title: Swiss Government Excellence PhD Scholarship 2027-28: India Deadline and Application
provider: Swiss Confederation, Federal Commission for Scholarships for Foreign Students
amount: CHF 2,450 per month for basic living expenses; up to 36 months, subject to renewal
eligibility: Indian citizens seeking full-time PhD research at an eligible Swiss institution. Applicants must have a master’s degree or equivalent by 31 July 2027 (30 June for ETH Zurich), have been born after 31 December 1991, and have a research plan and support letter from a qualified Swiss academic supervisor. Additional residence and prior-award exclusions apply; check the official rules before applying.
deadline: 10 November 2026, 11:59 pm Swiss local time (India applicants)
description:
Start with the supervisor, then the scholarship form. For an applicant from India, the Swiss government lists 10 November 2026 at 11:59 pm Swiss local time as the deadline for its 2027-28 PhD scholarship. A completed form without a Swiss supervisor’s support letter will not pass the published requirements. Read the official Asia country list for India’s deadline and available scholarship types.

What the PhD award covers

The Swiss Confederation offers CHF 2,450 a month towards one person’s basic living costs. This is a scholarship, not a salary or a promise to cover every expense. The PhD award starts on 1 September 2027 and is initially for 12 months. It may be renewed twice, up to 36 months in total, subject to academic progress. The award is for full-time research in Switzerland.

India’s listing includes both PhD scholarships and research fellowships. A research fellowship is a separate, shorter route for doctoral researchers who are pursuing a PhD in their home country. Check the official scholarship guide and select the route matching your research plan.

Check eligibility before approaching a host

For the PhD route, you need a master’s degree or equivalent completed by 31 July 2027, or by 30 June 2027 if your host is ETH Zurich. Applicants must have been born after 31 December 1991. Prepare a research proposal with a timeline and identify an academic supervisor in Switzerland who is authorised to guide the doctorate and willing to provide a support letter and short CV.

If you already live in Switzerland, the official conditions limit how early you may have entered. Previous Swiss Government Excellence Scholarship holders and applicants without a host supervisor are among those excluded. Admission to a Swiss doctoral programme is a separate process from the scholarship. Graduate-school applicants may also need an admission confirmation with the scholarship application, so read the official applicant FAQ for your route.

Apply through the Swiss government portal

  1. Read the country deadline and PhD eligibility on the official Swiss scholarship pages.

  2. Agree the research project with a suitable Swiss supervisor and obtain the required support letter.

  3. Use the Apply here link on the Swiss government guide to complete the eligibility check and register in Grants Online (GO ESKAS).

  4. Upload the research plan, degree records and other required documents, then submit before the India deadline in Swiss local time.

The scholarship application is free. The Swiss government warns against payment requests made in its name. Do not send an application by email or post. If you are comparing funding options, the DekhoCampus scholarship directory has other programmes to review.

Questions Indian applicants ask

Is the research fellowship the same as the PhD scholarship?

No. India is eligible for both. The PhD award supports a Swiss doctorate for up to 36 months with renewals; the research fellowship supports a shorter Swiss research stay during a PhD pursued in the home country.

Can I apply without a Swiss supervisor’s letter?

No. The Swiss government says scholarship applications without a Swiss academic supervisor and support letter will not be considered.

Does a scholarship application also admit me to a Swiss PhD programme?

No. Scholarship selection and university admission are separate. Check the host university’s admission rules as well as the scholarship rules.

title: Vikash Scholarship 2026-27: Repayment Terms and Hard-Copy Application
amount: Financial assistance; no fixed amount stated in the fresh form
eligibility: The current invitation covers financially disadvantaged, meritorious students of Odisha pursuing engineering diplomas or eligible undergraduate and postgraduate courses. The fresh form requires a government-recognised course at a recognised institute. Confirm any course-specific conditions with the trust; the form does not state a universal marks or income cutoff.
description:
Read the repayment undertaking before applying for Vikash Educational Charitable Trust’s 2026-27 scholarship. The fresh form asks students to promise that they will return the assistance, without interest, within five years of completing their course. A parent undertaking also appears in the form. Treat this as a financial commitment to understand, not as an automatically non-repayable grant.

The trust’s current invitation sets 30 November 2026 as the deadline for hard-copy applications with the required documents. Downloading or filling the form online does not complete submission.

Check the commitment with your parents

The student declaration says returned funds will support other students. The parent undertaking says the parent will encourage repayment and return the amount if the student fails to do so. Before signing, ask the trust how repayment would be arranged and how it handles circumstances that affect a student’s ability to repay. Do not assume a waiver, instalment schedule or exception that is not stated in your award terms.

The official fresh form for 2026-27 also provides for discontinuing assistance and seeking its return if information is false or the student is not sincere in their studies. Read the declarations as part of the application, rather than treating them as routine signature boxes.

Who the current invitation covers

Vikash Educational Charitable Trust is based in Bhubaneswar. Its 2026-27 call invites needy, meritorious students of Odisha pursuing an engineering diploma or undergraduate and postgraduate courses in fields including Humanities, Science, Commerce, Engineering, Medicine, BSc and GNM Nursing, and Agriculture.

The fresh form requires a government-recognised course in a recognised institute and asks whether the institution is government or private. It does not publish a single marks percentage or family-income ceiling for every applicant. Provide the academic and financial details requested, and contact the trust if your course or circumstances need clarification.

Plan around an award that has not yet been fixed

The fresh application does not state a standard amount payable to every selected student. Do not budget for a particular sum until the trust confirms your award. It asks for annual course fees, payments already made, family income and previous financial support, which you should enter accurately.

Previous assistance has a separate section covering school, higher-secondary and undergraduate study. Give the source, period and amount where applicable. Your college must also indicate whether you receive other assistance.

Use the fresh form and allow time for signatures

The official downloads page provides separate fresh and renewal forms. A new applicant should choose the 2026-27 fresh form. Fill it yourself, use capital letters in the sections that require them and complete all applicable fields. Ask the trust how to mark an item that does not apply instead of inventing an entry.

The application includes your declaration, the parent undertaking and a certificate signed by the principal with the college seal. It also asks for two unrelated people of standing in your locality who know your family. Obtain their consent before sharing their contact details.

Build the document packet before sending it

  • Admission or allotment letter and the relevant entrance rank card.

  • Your Aadhaar copy, income certificate from the Revenue Officer, and the caste and BPL or ration-card documents requested in the checklist.

  • Receipts for amounts paid to the college and the first page of your bank passbook.

  • Two passport-size photographs and marksheets for examinations already passed.

  • A personal account of your family’s financial situation and why you need assistance.

The personal account may be written in Odia or English. Explain the household’s income, education expenses and difficulties in your own words. Where a listed certificate does not apply to you, seek instructions from the trust before sending an incomplete packet.

Send the signed hard copy and attachments to Vikash Educational Charitable Trust, Rose Dale, 139 District Center, Chandrasekharpur, Bhubaneswar, Odisha 751016. The notice specifies submission by 30 November; it does not say that posting on the last day is sufficient. Allow delivery time and keep a copy of the full packet and your dispatch receipt.

For application or repayment questions, use the trust’s official email or its published contact number, 9337077785. You can compare other support options in the scholarship directory before making a commitment.

Questions before you sign

Is this assistance automatically non-repayable?

No. The fresh form contains a student promise to return the assistance without interest within five years of course completion, together with a parent undertaking. Ask the trust to clarify the terms before signing.

Can I apply simply by emailing the completed form?

The current instructions require a signed hard copy with the documents. The contact email is available for questions; it is not stated as a replacement for hard-copy submission.

How much money will every selected student receive?

The current fresh form does not give one fixed award amount. Obtain the trust’s award confirmation before relying on a sum to pay your fees.

title: Forrest Scholarship 2027: PhD Application and University Checks
amount: 2027 stipend: at least AUD 35,550 per year, plus other support
eligibility: Applicants must have applied for a full-time, campus-based PhD at a participating Western Australian university, hold a First Class Honours degree or equivalent, and not have started the proposed PhD or previously undertaken doctoral research. Residence at Forrest Hall is normally required; exemptions need approval. International applicants are eligible. Read the official eligibility and award conditions before applying.
description:
A Forrest Scholarship application does not replace your university application. For an Indian student planning a PhD in Western Australia, the practical first step is to check that both applications are moving forward.

Two applications to keep track of

The official 2027 application portal sets the Foundation deadline at 11:59 pm AWST on 30 October 2026. It also requires a separate PhD and Research Training Program scholarship, or equivalent, application to the intended university. University closing dates may differ.

Download the editable form and save it on your own device. The portal does not autosave it. If you use the Word version, convert the finished document to PDF before uploading. Keep a dated copy of your submission and a separate note of the university application status.

Check the conditions before comparing awards

The official scholarship conditions specify a minimum annual stipend of AUD 35,550 for 2027, with a higher amount possible through the enrolling university. International scholars also receive tuition-fee and overseas student health-cover support. Accommodation and other allowances have separate conditions; do not treat the package as an unrestricted cash payment.

The participating universities are Curtin, Edith Cowan, Murdoch, Notre Dame Australia’s Fremantle campus and the University of Western Australia. Confirm your proposed supervisor and research fit before committing to an application.

Files worth checking before submission

The portal asks for the completed application, a photograph, a CV of no more than four pages and academic transcripts. It warns that applications without the completed form and mentor or supervisor approval will not be considered. Check that every PDF opens and that your name is consistent across files.

Questions applicants ask

Does applying to the Foundation secure a university place?

No. The university admission and research-scholarship processes are separate. Follow the relevant university’s instructions as well as the Foundation’s.

Should I use an estimated rupee value to plan my budget?

Build your budget in Australian dollars first. Exchange rates change, and different parts of the award cover different costs. Ask the university what you would actually receive and which expenses remain yours.

Prepared by Geethika Reddy, DekhoCampus’s designated AI editor. The current-cycle deadline and application requirements were checked against the Foundation’s 2027 portal and published conditions on 23 October 2026.

title: Manipur Pre-Matric ST Scholarship 2026-27: Eligibility and NSP Deadline
provider: Manipur Directorate of Tribal Affairs and Hills
eligibility: For Scheduled Tribe students belonging to Manipur who are studying in Class 9 or 10 at a government or government-recognised school in India. The 2026-27 state notice sets the parent or guardian annual income ceiling at ₹2.5 lakh.
description:
Students from Manipur who are in Class 9 or 10 can apply for the state’s pre-matric ST scholarship through the National Scholarship Portal (NSP). The Directorate of Tribal Affairs and Hills opened the 2026-27 application window on 1 August 2026 and set 31 October 2026 as the last date for students to submit. This is the date in the official Manipur notification.

Who should check eligibility?

The notice invites Scheduled Tribe students belonging to Manipur whose parent or guardian earns no more than ₹2.5 lakh a year. They must study at a government or government-recognised school in India. This page concerns the pre-matric scheme for Classes 9 and 10, not the separate post-matric scheme. Families looking for other opportunities can also browse the DekhoCampus scholarship listings.

What to do before applying

Use the official NSP student portal for the application. Keep a mobile number and email address that the student can continue using. The Directorate also asks students to complete Aadhaar seeding and DBT activation for their bank account before submitting. Confirm those details with the bank rather than assuming an Aadhaar number on the account is sufficient.

Ask your school whether it is registered and ready to verify the NSP application. A submitted form still needs institutional verification. The state notice gives institutes until 20 November 2026 for that stage, but that later date is not extra time for students to apply.

Dates that matter

The dates below come from the Directorate’s 31 July 2026 notification. They describe different stages, so use the student deadline for your own submission.

Stage

2026-27 date

What it means

Student applications open

1 August 2026

Online applications start on NSP

Student submission closes

31 October 2026

Submit the application by this date

Defective application and institute verification

20 November 2026

Follow up promptly if corrections are requested

Source: Directorate of Tribal Affairs and Hills, Manipur, 2026-27 notification. The notice says the 31 October student deadline will not be extended.

A check that can prevent a rejected application

The Directorate says students at fully government-funded institutions that already provide free education, boarding, lodging and other educational facilities are not eligible under these schemes. If that sounds like your school, ask its scholarship nodal officer before applying. Do not choose a different institution category to work around the restriction.

Questions students ask

Is the income limit ₹2 lakh or ₹2.5 lakh?

For the 2026-27 Manipur application, the state notification states ₹2.5 lakh. Use the current official notice rather than an older general description.

Can I apply after 31 October if school verification is still open?

No. The 20 November verification date is for later processing. The student application deadline is 31 October 2026.

Where should I apply?

Apply through the official NSP student portal linked above. Check the scheme shown in your account before submitting.

title: Indira Gandhi Scholarship HP 2026-27: Merit Rules and Deadline
provider: Department of Higher Education, Himachal Pradesh
amount: ₹18,000 per year
eligibility: Bona fide Himachali students selected through the specified HPBOSE Class 12 or BA/BSc/BCom merit lists and continuing in an academic or professional course. Selection is not automatic at 60%; subsequent-class performance governs renewal. No family-income ceiling.
description:
Himachal Pradesh's Indira Gandhi Utkrisht Chatravriti Yojana supports students selected on academic merit after Class 12 or a BA, BSc or BCom degree. The award is ₹18,000 a year. For 2026-27, the National Scholarship Portal scheme list gives 31 October 2026 as the student application deadline.

Your first check should be your place in the relevant merit list, not just your percentage. This is a selective merit scholarship, not an automatic payment to everyone who passes with 60%.

Which merit list matters?

The Himachal Pradesh Education Department's scheme rules describe two entry routes for bona fide Himachali students:

  • After Class 12: ten toppers each from the Arts, Science and Commerce merit lists supplied by HPBOSE, provided they continue in an academic or professional course.

  • After graduation: ten toppers from the BA, BSc and BCom merit lists, provided they move into an academic or professional course.

Ask your institution's scholarship officer how your merit position and admission will be confirmed for the relevant route. A high score alone should not be treated as a selection letter. The department specifies no family-income ceiling for this scheme.

Annual support and the renewal condition

The current rate is ₹18,000 per year. The official scheme specifications and rate-revision notification contain the award rules. The revised rate replaces the older ₹10,000 figure in the original approval.

The scheme provides for yearly renewal through completion of the degree or course. Its rules set a 60% requirement in subsequent classes. Do not confuse that continuation condition with a promise that any applicant scoring 60% will receive a fresh award. Keep your latest result and enrolment record ready when applying for renewal.

Use the student deadline, not the verification date

NSP lists separate dates for applicants and the officials who verify their forms. The later dates do not give students extra time to submit a new application.

Stage

Closing date in 2026

Student application

31 October

Defective-application and institute verification

17 November

DNO/SNO/MNO verification

18 November

To locate these dates in the official scheme list, choose State of Himachal Pradesh and find Indira Gandhi Utkrisht Chatravriti Yojana, marked as a merit-based scheme for academic year 2026-27.

Apply through NSP and keep the acknowledgement

Start from the NSP Students page. One Time Registration is mandatory. Use your OTR ID and password under Apply For Scholarship to access the fresh or renewal application, then follow the requirements shown for your course and scheme.

Have your Himachal domicile evidence, qualifying examination result and current admission details available. Upload the documents actually requested in the application. A general document checklist is not a reason to assume that this merit scheme has an income ceiling or requires every category certificate.

Review your entries before submission, save the acknowledgement and monitor the application for verification queries. If you cannot locate the scheme or your merit record, contact your institution's scholarship officer before the deadline.

The Apply Now button on this website opens a counselling enquiry form. That enquiry is not your scholarship application; you can go directly to the NSP Students link above to apply.

Comparing another Himachal merit scholarship?

Girls who have completed HPBOSE Class 12 can also read the Kalpana Chawla scholarship's selection and renewal rules. The two schemes have different merit criteria. NSP's Students page allows an application for one merit-based scheme in 2026-27, so check your eligibility before choosing rather than submitting both as interchangeable options.

Frequently asked questions

Is this scholarship open to every student with 60%?

No. Fresh selection follows the specified merit-list routes. The scheme's 60% condition concerns subsequent classes; it does not replace the topper-selection requirement.

Can a graduate apply?

The rules include toppers from BA, BSc and BCom merit lists who join a further academic or professional course. Confirm your applicable merit list and admission with your institution.

Is there a family-income limit?

The Education Department states that selection is based on merit without an income ceiling.

How much does a selected student receive?

The revised award is ₹18,000 a year. Renewal remains subject to the scheme's academic and continuation requirements.

Can I wait until 17 November to apply?

No. The student application deadline is 31 October 2026. The November dates are for verification and do not extend the student application window.

title: DNHDD Post-Matric SC Scholarship 2026-27: Apply by 31 October
provider: Government of Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu
amount: Fee support and study allowance, subject to sanction
eligibility: Indian students belonging to Scheduled Castes and domiciled in Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu, studying a recognised post-matric course in India. The scheme guidelines linked on NSP set the parent or guardian income ceiling at ₹2.5 lakh a year. Confirm your course and institution eligibility before submitting.
description:
Submit before the student deadline

The National Scholarship Portal lists the DNHDD post-matric scheme for SC students as open for 2026-27. Student applications close on 31 October 2026. The later verification windows are for processing applications; they do not extend the student submission deadline.

  • Student applications: until 31 October 2026.

  • Defective-application and institute verification: until 15 November 2026.

  • DNO/SNO/MNO verification: until 30 November 2026.

You can find this entry under Centrally Sponsored Schemes, then UT of The Dadra Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu, on the official NSP scheme list.

Check your course and domicile

This route is for SC students domiciled in the Union Territory, rather than everyone attending a college there. The linked guidelines cover recognised post-matric study in India, including Classes 11 and 12 and eligible diploma, undergraduate and postgraduate courses. They set an annual parent or guardian income ceiling of ₹2.5 lakh.

Ask your institution to confirm the scheme mapping if you are studying outside the Union Territory, changing courses or applying for another qualification at a level you have already completed. Do not select a similar-looking scheme merely to finish the form.

Understand the financial support

The scheme provides support for eligible compulsory non-refundable fees and study expenses. The amount depends on your course group and circumstances, including whether you are a day scholar or hosteller. It is not one fixed payment for every applicant.

Before committing to a fee payment, ask your scholarship nodal officer for the applicable 2026-27 award and covered fee heads. The specification currently linked by NSP carries an April 2018 effective date, so its older allowance figures should not be treated as a personalised payment guarantee. The sanctioning authority determines the final entitlement.

Prepare a complete application

Start from the NSP student portal and follow the registration or login instructions shown there. Have these records available so you can respond to the form and your institution:

  • Domicile and SC certificates.

  • The income certificate applicable to your application.

  • Your previous examination marksheet and current admission details.

  • Course, institution and fee records.

  • Your own bank details and any identity documents requested by NSP.

Use the document list displayed for your scheme as the final upload checklist. Match your name, course year and institution details across the form and supporting records. Preview every field, submit the application and retain its acknowledgement. A saved draft alone does not complete submission.

Follow up after submission

Check your NSP account for a defect or verification message and speak to your institution promptly if a correction is requested. Keep the acknowledgement and copies of uploaded records. Do not assume that institute verification means the money has already been sanctioned or transferred.

If you also receive another scholarship or stipend, disclose it to the institution before accepting overlapping support. For other funding routes at different study levels, explore the DekhoCampus scholarship directory.

Frequently asked questions

Can I apply until 15 November 2026?

The student application deadline is 31 October 2026. The 15 November date is the listed defective-application and institute verification deadline, not a general extension for new applications.

Does studying in Daman make me eligible?

Not by itself. This scheme is linked to DNHDD domicile and SC status, along with the income, course and institution conditions. Confirm your domicile route before selecting the scheme.

Will every student receive the same scholarship amount?

No. Course classification, eligible fees and individual circumstances affect support. Ask the institution to confirm the amount applicable to your course before relying on a particular figure.

The scholarship supports eligible study after Class 10. Financial assistance depends on the recognised course, applicable fees and student circumstances. Confirm the award payable for your course with the institution before planning your fees around it. An application is not a scholarship sanction.

title: Kerala IWCS Scholarship 2026-27: ₹15,000 for CA, CMA and CS Students
provider: Directorate of Minority Welfare, Government of Kerala
amount: ₹15,000 one-time award
eligibility:
Applicants must be Kerala permanent residents studying in Kerala and belong to Muslim, Christian, Sikh, Buddhist, Jain or Parsi communities. The scheme covers intermediate and final-stage CA, CMA and CS students. Intermediate students need at least 60% in Foundation or graduation; final-stage students must have passed Intermediate.

BPL applicants receive priority. In their absence, APL applicants with annual family income up to ₹8 lakh may be considered. Selection considers merit and income. Previous recipients of this departmental scholarship must not apply again.
description:
Match your documents to your course stage

Keep the pass certificate for your previous stage and proof of admission to your current stage together. For example, a final-stage applicant needs the Intermediate pass certificate and evidence of joining the final course. Also prepare the course registration and fee records requested in the notice.

Before uploading, open each scan at normal reading size. Check that the student’s name, course stage and result are legible. Give the files clear names so you can distinguish a registration receipt from a pass certificate when attaching them.

Finish both parts of the application

Use the official Minority Welfare portal to register or log in. Complete your profile and qualifications, select the scholarship and upload the required records. Check the personal, academic and bank entries before submitting; the portal warns that editing may not be available afterwards.

Online submission alone is insufficient. Deliver or post the registration printout and supporting documents to the Directorate of Minority Welfare, Fourth Floor, Vikas Bhavan, Thiruvananthapuram, by 30 November 2026. Use the address and document checklist in the official notice when preparing the packet.

Work backwards from the arrival deadline. Allow time for printing, checking the enclosures and delivery. Keep a copy of the complete packet and any delivery acknowledgement with your online application reference.

Check the bank and supporting records

The award requires an account in the student’s own name. Compare the account number, IFSC and branch details with the passbook. The notice’s checklist also covers academic marksheets, Aadhaar, nativity, community or minority proof, income certificate and ration card. Follow the full checklist rather than relying only on the files visible in the first upload screen.

Questions about the IWCS application

Is the ₹15,000 award renewed each year?

No. The official notice describes it as a one-time award and excludes previous recipients of this scholarship.

Can I use the same qualification rule for intermediate and final studies?

No. Check the rule for the stage you are currently pursuing and attach the corresponding pass and admission records.

How can I avoid missing the hard-copy step?

Set a separate reminder for preparing and delivering the packet. Keep its delivery record alongside the online submission acknowledgement.

If you are comparing support options, use the scholarship directory and read each programme’s eligibility separately.

The report is evidence that the programme exists, not a notice for a new round. Do not use figures or selection rules from a past year as if they apply now.

How to decide whether to follow the next round

Start with your present course and the reason education costs are difficult to meet. Keep enrolment proof, recent marksheets and documents explaining the family’s financial circumstances ready. Those records may help you compare the next official eligibility notice with your situation. Do not submit private documents to a link circulated in a message before checking that it belongs to a verified application process.

title: Himachal Pradesh ST Post-Matric Scholarship 2026-27: Eligibility and Last Date
provider: Government of Himachal Pradesh and Ministry of Tribal Affairs
amount: ₹230 to ₹1,200 per month plus eligible fees
eligibility: ST students domiciled in Himachal Pradesh, pursuing eligible recognised post-matric study in India, with annual family income not exceeding ₹2.5 lakh. Institution, course and other scheme conditions apply.
level: Class 11 / Class 12 / Diploma / UG / PG / Research
description:
ST students domiciled in Himachal Pradesh can apply for the 2026-27 post-matric scholarship on NSP until 31 October 2026. The scheme helps with eligible course fees and a maintenance allowance after Class 10. You do not need to be in your first year to consider it: the rules also allow an eligible student who missed the first-year application to apply later for the remaining course period.

Check domicile, income and the course together

The core requirements are Scheduled Tribe status in the domicile state, a recognised qualifying examination and an eligible post-matric course in India. Annual family income must not exceed ₹2.5 lakh. The official ST post-matric scholarship rules set out the institution categories and income calculation.

Before you fill the form, ask your scholarship office to confirm the exact course entry used on NSP. A similar course name is not enough if the institution or programme is not eligible. Students at institutions covered by the separate Top Class ST scholarship should also confirm which scheme applies to them.

This is a different programme from the Thakur Sen Negi scholarship based on HPBOSE matric merit. Do not use that programme’s merit shortlist to decide whether you can apply here.

What the scholarship pays

The Ministry of Tribal Affairs describes two parts of the award: approved compulsory fees, subject to the applicable state limits, and a monthly allowance. The NSP-linked award schedule lists maintenance rates from ₹230 to ₹1,200 a month, depending on course group and hosteller or day-scholar status. Payment is limited to the eligible study period, with a maximum of ten months in the academic year.

The top rate is not a flat award for everyone. Ask for your course group and accommodation classification before making a budget. Keep your fee statement and any required hostel certification ready; a rented room should not automatically be entered as an approved hostel.

31 October is the deadline for your application

The NSP scheme directory, under Himachal Pradesh, separates student submission from the checks that follow. These are the dates shown for the ST post-matric scheme in 2026-27.

Stage

Closing date

Student application

31 October 2026

Defective-application and institute verification

17 November 2026

DNO/SNO/MNO verification

18 November 2026

Do not wait for the November dates to start a new form. After submitting, keep checking for a defect message and contact the institution promptly if your application needs attention.

Prepare a complete application, not just an OTR

Start at the official NSP student portal. One Time Registration is required, but it is separate from submitting the scholarship application. Log in through the scholarship option, choose the correct fresh or renewal route and review the scheme name before proceeding.

Keep your domicile and ST certificates, income certificate, academic records, photograph and bank details together. Add disability documentation where applicable, and follow the upload requirements displayed for your profile. Check that every scan can be read at normal size and that the bank account details match your own active account.

Save the application reference and submitted form. If your institution is missing from the options, contact its scholarship office rather than selecting another college. Tell the office about any other scholarship you receive so it can advise on the applicable combination rules.

Continuing students: choose the right route

A later-year first application is different from renewal of an existing award. Under the guidelines, a student who did not apply in the first year can seek support from the application stage for the remaining duration, subject to eligibility. That provision does not promise arrears for the missed year.

Renewal normally depends on progression to the next class and satisfactory attendance and conduct. If your result involves a backlog, promotion rule or a missed examination, take the result and supporting documents to the institute before choosing an answer in the form.

Questions about the HP ST post-matric scholarship

Can I apply while studying outside Himachal Pradesh?

Yes, eligible study outside the state is allowed. Your domicile remains relevant, and the institution and course must satisfy the scheme’s requirements. Confirm their eligibility with the scholarship office.

Is the highest maintenance amount guaranteed?

No. The rate depends on your course group and residence category. Fee support is a separate component subject to the applicable rules.

I missed the first year. Is it too late for the entire course?

Not necessarily. The guidelines allow a first application in a later year for the remaining eligible period. Apply within the current student window rather than assuming that you must wait for another admission.

Does completing OTR finish my application?

No. OTR gives you the registration needed to use NSP. You must still complete and submit the scholarship form, then follow its verification status.

title: IAEA Marie Curie Fellowship 2026: Funding and How to Apply
amount: Up to €20,000 for tuition and €20,000 for living costs
eligibility: Women from IAEA Member States who have been accepted into, or are enrolled in, a nuclear-related master’s programme at an accredited university can apply. Indian applicants meet the member-state condition. IAEA gives preference to academic results of 75% or above, or a GPA above 3.0 out of 4.0; it describes these results as a preference, not a universal minimum admission cutoff.
description:
Start with your master’s admission

This fellowship is for women who already have admission to, or are studying in, a nuclear-related master’s programme. It does not replace a university application or provide a place on a course. Before starting the fellowship form, check that your university letter identifies the subject and duration of your programme.

The scheme accepts applicants from IAEA Member States. India is an IAEA member, so Indian nationality meets that part of the eligibility rules. You still need to satisfy the course and university requirements.

Which subjects fit the fellowship?

IAEA supports study connected with peaceful nuclear science and technology. Examples include nuclear engineering, nuclear physics and chemistry, nuclear medicine, radiation biology, isotopic techniques, nuclear safety and security, non-proliferation, and nuclear law.

A degree title alone may not explain the connection. Read the official examples of supported fields alongside your course description. In your application, explain how the programme relates to the nuclear field and the work you want to do after graduating.

The academic preference is 75% or above, or a GPA greater than 3.0 on a four-point scale. The provider presents this as a selection preference. Do not treat a locally converted percentage as an official equivalence unless your university can substantiate it.

Budget with two separate funding limits

The award can provide up to €20,000 towards tuition and up to €20,000 towards living costs for the master’s programme. These are maximum amounts, not an annual allowance or a promise that every expense will be paid. Keep your tuition estimate separate from accommodation and other living costs when assessing the funding gap.

Other scholarships must be disclosed with supporting documents. The current provider guidance says IAEA support is reduced where additional scholarship funding exists, with tuition support rather than living-cost support in that situation. Read the individual award offer before committing to expenses.

The programme also offers limited internship opportunities facilitated by IAEA. A fellowship application should not be treated as a guaranteed internship or job placement.

Arrange your reference before the deadline

Use the document list on the official information-for-applicants page to prepare:

  • A passport or national identity document.

  • The university’s official admission or acceptance letter showing the nuclear-related field and course duration.

  • A tuition-fee statement or confirmation of tuition costs.

  • Details and evidence of other scholarships, where applicable.

  • At least one completed reference using the IAEA template; a second reference is preferred.

Your referee must send the completed applicant reference form directly to MSCFP@iaea.org by the application deadline. Ask early and confirm that the form has been sent. Uploading your own application does not complete this separate reference step.

Application documents must be in English. If you provide a document in another language, include an official English translation. Incomplete applications are not considered.

Submit through IAEA’s application system

  1. Open the 2026 fellowship call on IAEA’s application portal.

  2. Select the 2026 call, identified as TAL-MSCFP-C7FLW-2026, and follow the account and application instructions.

  3. Complete the form, attach the requested evidence and review the details before submission.

  4. Finish by 31 October 2026 and keep your submission confirmation. Check the portal’s displayed closing time and time zone rather than assuming midnight in India.

  5. Monitor your email for the selection decision and any further instructions.

The selection committee considers academic background, achievements, motivation, career goals and commitment to public service, alongside diversity factors. Make your explanation specific to your studies and planned work instead of listing general ambitions.

Read the award obligations before accepting

Selected applicants are asked to confirm acceptance within one week. The offer sets out payment arrangements, commitments and administrative requirements. Recipients are expected to complete the master’s programme. Failure to graduate or meet the scholarship requirements can end the award and lead to a request to repay tuition and living-cost support.

Questions for Indian applicants

Can I apply before receiving university admission?

The published criteria require acceptance or enrolment, and the document list includes an official university admission letter. Secure that evidence before submitting the fellowship application.

Is €40,000 paid every year?

No. The published limits are up to €20,000 for tuition and up to €20,000 for living costs for the master’s programme. The individual offer determines the actual support.

Do I need two references?

One reference is mandatory; a second is preferred. Referees must use the provider’s template and send it directly to IAEA by the deadline.

What if my master’s has no nuclear-related component?

This fellowship is subject-specific. For a different postgraduate programme in India, you can also read the separate UGC postgraduate scholarship guide and assess its distinct eligibility rules.

At least one reference is mandatory and a second is preferred. Declare any other scholarship funding, as it can reduce the IAEA award. Selection is competitive and applicants are informed by email.

title: Vidyasamunnathi Entrance Coaching Assistance 2026-27: Marks and Fee Rules
provider: Kerala State Welfare Corporation for Forward Communities
amount: Coaching-fee reimbursement up to ₹10,000
eligibility:
Applicants must belong to a non-reserved forward community of Kerala, have annual family income below ₹4 lakh and attend eligible classroom coaching for medical, engineering, law or CUET entrance examinations. Online coaching is excluded. The marks requirements vary by coaching category and qualification; check the detailed table below.

The undergraduate category has an upper age limit of 20 years. Postgraduate applicants need at least 60% in their completed degree, with no age limit stated. Previous recipients of this entrance-coaching assistance cannot apply again. An active savings account in the applicant's own name is required.
description:
Before applying for Vidyasamunnathi entrance-coaching assistance 2026-27, check the marks rule for your category. The scheme can reimburse eligible coaching fees up to ₹10,000, but medical and engineering applicants do not have the same academic threshold as law and CUET applicants. The online application deadline is 7 November 2026.

Match your coaching category to your qualification

The official entrance-coaching guidelines distinguish undergraduate preparation from postgraduate preparation. For medical and engineering coaching, the subject-wise requirement depends on whether the applicant has completed SSLC or higher secondary.

Coaching category

Academic requirement

UG medical or engineering, after SSLC

B+ grade or at least 70% in each of Physics, Chemistry, Biology and Mathematics

UG medical or engineering, after HSS

B+ grade or at least 70% in each of Physics, Chemistry and the optional subject

UG law or CUET

B grade or at least 60% in HSS or an equivalent examination

Postgraduate entrance coaching

Completed undergraduate degree with at least 60% marks

The undergraduate category has an upper age limit of 20 years. No age limit is prescribed for the postgraduate category. The document does not specify an age-calculation date, so applicants near the limit should ask Samunnathi before submitting.

Check the household and classroom conditions

You must belong to a non-reserved forward community of Kerala, with annual family income below ₹4 lakh. Use a family-income certificate issued by the Village Officer. It must be in the name of the applicant, parent or guardian who appears on the ration card containing the applicant's name. An individual-income certificate is not accepted.

You must be attending the entrance-coaching programme in person at an eligible institute. Online coaching is excluded. Applicants who previously received this entrance-coaching assistance from the corporation cannot apply again.

The award reimburses fees paid, up to ₹10,000; it is not an automatic ₹10,000 payment. Lower-income applicants receive priority, and selection depends on available funds. Keep an active savings account in your own name at a nationalised or scheduled bank and check its payment details carefully.

Get the institute certificate and scans ready

Ask your institute to complete the prescribed 2026-27 entrance-coaching certificate. It records the programme and level, enrolment number, coaching duration and fees paid during January to December 2026. The head or authorised signatory must add a signature, phone number and office seal, along with the institute's recognition and registration details.

Prepare readable scans of:

  • Caste proof: the Village Officer's certificate recording caste, or the SSLC page showing the caste entry.

  • The family-income certificate and pages 1 and 2 of the ration card containing your name.

  • The relevant SSLC, HSS, equivalent or degree certificate showing marks.

  • The prescribed coaching certificate.

  • The first page of your bank passbook, showing the account number, IFSC and branch.

  • The basic qualification certificate for the relevant examination and a copy of your SSLC certificate.

Retain the original coaching-fee receipt. The guidelines require shortlisted applicants to provide the original receipt for fees paid between 1 January and 31 December 2026, with the institute's GST registration number. That receipt period does not extend the 7 November application deadline.

Apply online, then follow any shortlist message

Use the official Samunnathi portal. Register and complete your profile if you are a new user; existing users can sign in with their registered username and password. Choose the correct entrance-coaching category, upload the required scans, review the details and submit by the deadline. Keep a copy of the application.

Do not post documents immediately after applying online. Only shortlisted applicants who receive an SMS or email should send the requested papers, including the application copy and original fee receipt. Follow that message and the address in the guidelines: Kerala State Welfare Corporation for Forward Communities Ltd, TC9/476, L2, Kuleena, Jawahar Nagar, Kowdiar P.O., Thiruvananthapuram-3.

For a question about your marks, age or documents, contact Samunnathi on 0471-2311215 or 6238170312. Incomplete forms, incorrect details or unclear uploads can lead to rejection.

Entrance-coaching assistance FAQs

Can I claim this assistance for an online NEET coaching course?

No. The guidelines require in-person coaching and exclude online training, even when the entrance examination is covered.

Is an overall 70% enough for medical or engineering coaching?

The undergraduate rule specifies subject-wise marks. SSLC applicants need B+ or at least 70% in each of Physics, Chemistry, Biology and Mathematics; HSS applicants need that threshold in Physics, Chemistry and the optional subject.

Does the 20-year age limit apply to postgraduate coaching?

No. The guidelines state an upper age limit of 20 years for the undergraduate category and no age limit for postgraduate applicants, who need at least 60% in their completed degree.

Should I send the original receipt as soon as I apply?

No. Keep it safely and send it only after receiving the shortlist SMS or email requesting documents. The receipt must carry the coaching institute's GST registration number.

Applicants preparing for recruitment examinations should read the separate Bank, PSC and SSC coaching-assistance guide. Browse the scholarship directory for other support.

title: Top Class Education Scholarship for SC Students 2026-27: Eligibility and NSP Dates

The Top Class Education Scholarship for Scheduled Caste students supports study beyond Class 12 at institutions notified by the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment. Read the exact current portal specifications before assuming you qualify. The National Scholarship Portal lists student applications for 2026-27 until 31 October 2026.
description:
What makes this different from a standard post-matric award?

Two SC students in the same course may not have the same outcome under this scheme. The Ministry-linked guidelines restrict fresh awards to first-year students in notified institutions and allocate slots by institution and course. If you are already in a later year, check whether you are seeking renewal rather than a fresh award. Your institution’s scholarship office can confirm whether it has a slot for your course.

title: Vidyasamunnathi CA, CS and CMA Scholarship 2026-27: Eligibility and Documents
provider: Kerala State Welfare Corporation for Forward Communities
amount: ₹10,000 for selected students
eligibility:
For students from non-reserved forward communities of Kerala pursuing CA, CS or CMA (ICWA). Applicants must have passed CA/CMA Intermediate or the CS Executive Programme, with fewer than four years elapsed since passing that stage. Annual family income must not exceed ₹4 lakh, and applicants must be under 35 on the date applications are invited.

An active bank account in the student's own name is required. Students receiving another central or state government scholarship or stipend, or who have already received this category's scholarship twice or more, are ineligible.
description:
Students pursuing CA, CS or CMA can apply for the Vidyasamunnathi Scholarship 2026-27 by 7 November 2026. Selected applicants receive ₹10,000. Passing the required intermediate or executive stage is essential: enrolment in the course alone does not meet the academic condition.

Check the stage you have completed

The official CA, CS and CMA guidelines cover courses conducted by the relevant professional institutes or recognised institutions. You must have passed CA/CMA Intermediate or the CS Executive Programme, and four years must not have elapsed since passing that level.

Applicants must belong to a non-reserved forward community of Kerala. Annual family income from all sources must be no more than ₹4 lakh. You must also be under 35 on the date applications are invited, rather than using the submission deadline to calculate your age.

How the ₹10,000 award is allocated

The guidelines provide for 60 scholarships, subject to funding. Lower-income applicants receive priority, so meeting the eligibility rules does not guarantee selection. Payment is made to an active account in the student's own name at a nationalised or scheduled bank.

You cannot apply if you receive another central or state government scholarship or stipend. Students who have already received this scholarship under the same category twice or more are also excluded.

Prepare these documents before you start

  • Proof of passing the required Intermediate examination or CS Executive Programme.

  • Your registration or enrolment card.

  • A family-income certificate issued by the Village Officer. It must be in the name of the applicant, parent or guardian included in the ration card containing the applicant's name. An individual-income certificate is not accepted.

  • The Village Officer's caste certificate or the SSLC page showing the caste entry.

  • The bank passbook's first page, with account number, IFSC and branch clearly readable.

  • Pages 1 and 2 of the ration card containing your name, and the first page of your SSLC certificate.

Compare the bank details in the form with the passbook before submitting. Incorrect account details, unclear scans or an incomplete application can prevent the application from being accepted or the payment from reaching you.

Submit a fresh application online

Open the official Samunnathi application portal. New applicants register and create a profile; returning applicants can use their existing login. Select the appropriate scholarship category, complete the form and upload the required documents.

Submit a new application for 2026-27 even if you applied previously. Retain a copy for your records. These guidelines do not require you to post the application and document copies to the corporation. For help with an eligibility or portal issue, contact Samunnathi on 0471-2311215 or 6238170312.

Questions about this scholarship

Can a foundation-stage student apply?

Not on the basis of foundation enrolment alone. The academic rule requires CA/CMA Intermediate or the CS Executive Programme to have been passed, within the stated four-year limit.

Can I use a parent's bank account?

No. The guidelines require an active bank account in the student's own name.

Can I receive the award for a third time?

No. Applicants who have received this category's scholarship twice or more in previous years are not eligible to apply again.

Does last year's application carry forward?

No. Your login can be reused, but a separate scholarship application is required for each year.

For other study levels, compare the separate Vidyasamunnathi graduation scholarship or browse the scholarship directory. Each category has its own eligibility conditions.

title: Griffith Vice Chancellor’s Scholarship 2027: 50% Tuition and Intake Deadlines
amount: 50% of eligible tuition fees
eligibility: New international students entering an eligible full-time undergraduate or postgraduate coursework degree in 2027. Applicants need an offer by the scholarship deadline, a previous-study GPA of at least 6.0/7 or equivalent, and must meet the course’s academic and English requirements. deadline: 28 November 2026 for Trimester 1; other intake dates below
description:
Griffith University’s Vice Chancellor’s International Scholarship can reduce eligible tuition fees by half for a new undergraduate or postgraduate coursework student. For the March 2027 intake, most applicants must apply by 28 November 2026. Secure your course offer before that deadline: a scholarship application alone does not secure admission.

Match the deadline to your intake

The university publishes separate dates for each group. The January deadline is specifically for students completing Australian Year 12; it is not a general extension for applicants studying in India.

Starting group

Use the university’s scholarship dates and terms when choosing your round. Awards are competitive and limited; meeting the minimum criteria does not guarantee selection.

Check your offer and course before applying

You must be a citizen of a country other than Australia or New Zealand and a new full-time student paying international fees. Previous study must meet a GPA of at least 6.0 on a seven-point scale, or the accepted equivalent. Your chosen degree’s academic and English-language requirements still apply.

The application form accepts a conditional or unconditional offer. Check any outstanding conditions in your offer rather than assuming that scholarship eligibility removes them.

Excluded study includes research degrees, online-campus programmes, diplomas, non-award and study-abroad courses, the Masters Qualifying Program, MBA programme code 5158, Griffith English Language Institute courses, part-time-only programmes and courses delivered with a partner organisation. Match the exact programme on your offer against these exclusions.

Budget for the portion you still pay

The award reduces eligible tuition by 50%; it is not a full-cost scholarship or a cash living allowance. Plan separately for the remaining tuition, accommodation, travel and other study costs. Tuition deductions are applied by each trimester’s census date while you remain eligible, and the balance is payable by that date.

Support follows the first degree’s length stated in the offer, reduced by any credit for previous study. Scholarship deferral is not allowed. Recipients must accept both the course and scholarship offers within their stated deadlines.

Prepare the application in the right order

  1. Apply for admission to Griffith and obtain your offer.

  2. Gather certified or attested copies of academic certificates and transcripts.

  3. Write a personal statement of 250-500 words explaining your course choice, reasons for seeking support and intended impact after graduation. Include evidence of relevant achievements.

  4. Complete the official scholarship form for the correct intake, using your Griffith ID and programme details.

Grades matter after selection too

Recipients must pass every course each trimester, progress to the next trimester and maintain an annual cumulative GPA of at least 5.5/7. Full-time enrolment, programme progress and student-visa requirements also apply, subject to the university’s stated credit exception. Changing international fee-paying status ends eligibility. Read the ongoing conditions before accepting the award.

For other funding options, explore the DekhoCampus scholarship directory.

Questions before applying

Can an Indian student apply without a Griffith offer?

No. You need a conditional or unconditional offer by the relevant scholarship closing date. Start with admission if you do not yet have one.

Does the 50% award cover accommodation?

No. The published award applies to eligible tuition fees. Arrange funds separately for living and other expenses.

Can I use the January deadline after finishing Class 12 in India?

That special round is for students completing Australian Year 12. Other Trimester 1 applicants should use 28 November 2026.

Is the scholarship automatic at a GPA of 6.0?

No. That is an application threshold. A university panel assesses eligible applications, and the number of awards is limited.

title: Leiden Excellence Scholarship: Tuition Support and 1 December Deadline
amount: €10,000 to €19,000 towards tuition

Start with the course, then check the award

The Leiden University Excellence Scholarship supports eligible full-time master’s programmes starting in September. Indian passport holders can meet the nationality condition, but nationality alone does not establish eligibility. Your course, academic record and access to Dutch government student finance also matter.

Leiden uses a top-10% academic standing as an indication of competitiveness, not a requirement to upload ranking proof. Applicants who already hold a Leiden master’s degree are generally excluded, with exceptions for programmes requiring a specified earlier master’s qualification or work experience.

Calculate the amount you would still need

The five tuition contributions are €10,000, €15,000, €17,500, €18,500 and €19,000. The award runs for the study programme’s duration and its level cannot be negotiated. This is partial funding: non-EEA recipients still need to demonstrate sufficient funds for their visa or residence permit.

Build two budgets before committing to a course. One should assume no scholarship; the other can show the effect of an award. Include remaining tuition, accommodation, travel and day-to-day spending. Do not treat the largest advertised contribution as an amount you will receive.

A full external scholarship cannot be combined with LExS. Ask the Scholarships Team before relying on a combination with a partial external award.

Submit two applications, not one

  1. Follow Leiden’s admission and application guidance for your master’s course, including any applicable application fee.

  2. After submitting admission, return to the Apply screen and open Scholarships. Eligible applicants should see LExS there.

  3. Upload a PDF motivation letter of no more than 500 words and submit the scholarship application before the deadline.

Leiden says creating and submitting the admission application can take up to three working days. A missing scholarship option can mean the admission application has not been submitted, the deadline has passed or the applicant is ineligible. Check those points before starting another application.

Review the PDF and every answer before final submission. Changes cannot be made afterwards through the portal or by emailing extra material. If you seek LExS for more than one programme or specialisation, each admission application needs its own scholarship application and motivation letter.

Make your motivation letter specific

Choose evidence that connects your previous study to the course you want to take. Explain what you have done, why the programme suits your academic plans and why you are seeking the award. A focused example is more useful than a long list of unsupported claims. Check the final PDF’s word count and legibility yourself.

Read the official LExS rules before submitting. For other funding options, compare the eligible course and country in the DekhoCampus scholarship directory.

Application questions

Does applying for admission automatically apply me for LExS?

No. Submit the separate scholarship application from the Scholarships section after submitting admission.

Can the award cover all my study and living costs?

No. It is a tuition contribution, and you must arrange the remaining costs and meet the applicable proof-of-funds requirement.

Can I submit for a February-start programme?

No. February starts are excluded from this scholarship.

title: Vidyasamunnathi High School Scholarship 2026-27: Kerala Eligibility and 7 November Deadline
provider: Kerala State Welfare Corporation for Forward Communities
amount: ₹2,500 per year
eligibility: For students in Classes 8, 9 or 10 at government or government-aided schools in Kerala who belong to economically disadvantaged forward communities. The 2026-27 high school guidelines specify annual family income up to ₹4 lakh and at least 70% marks in the previous annual examination. Read the official category guidelines for community and document requirements.
description:
Studying in Class 8, 9 or 10 at a Kerala government or government-aided school? Vidyasamunnathi may help with school costs if you meet the forward-community, income and marks rules. The 2026-27 high school application closes on 7 November 2026, so check the category guidelines before starting the online form.

Who can apply for the high school category?

The Kerala State Welfare Corporation for Forward Communities runs Vidyasamunnathi for economically disadvantaged students from forward communities. For the high school category, the 2026-27 guidelines cover Classes 8 to 10 in government and government-aided schools. They set a family income ceiling of ₹4 lakh a year and require at least 70% marks in the previous annual examination. Confirm that your community and school qualify under the official high school guidelines before uploading documents.

What is the award and deadline?

The high school scholarship amount is ₹2,500 for the year. The corporation’s 2026-27 application notice says online applications opened on 8 October 2026 and the last date for online submission is 7 November 2026. This deadline applies to the announced cycle; a later cycle needs a fresh official notice.

How to apply without choosing the wrong category

  1. Open the official Vidyasamunnathi portal and read the current high school guidelines.

  2. Register or sign in, then complete the applicant profile and select the high school scholarship category.

  3. Enter details that match your school, marks and income documents. Upload the files requested by the portal.

  4. Review the form and submit it online before 7 November 2026. Save the acknowledgement for follow-up.

The portal is the application route. DekhoCampus does not collect or submit scholarship applications. You can browse other scholarships if this category does not fit your school year.

Questions students ask

Can Class 7 students apply for this high school category?

No. The 2026-27 high school category covers Classes 8, 9 and 10.

Is the ₹2,500 a monthly amount?

No. The high school category lists ₹2,500 for the year.

Can I apply through DekhoCampus?

No. Submit through the corporation’s official portal. Use the linked guidelines to check documents and eligibility before filling the form.

title: Vidyasamunnathi Diploma Scholarship 2026-27: Course and Admission Rules
provider: Kerala State Welfare Corporation for Forward Communities
amount: ₹6,000 for the academic year
eligibility:
Applicants must belong to a non-reserved forward community of Kerala and take a regular, full-time diploma or certificate course lasting at least one year at an eligible institution. SSLC or equivalent marks must be at least 60%, or a B grade. Annual family income must not exceed ₹4 lakh. Applicants must be under 25 on the date applications are invited.

For study outside Kerala, admission must be through a national-level competitive examination. An institution's own entrance test does not qualify. Other central or state government scholarships or stipends are excluded, with an exception for e-grantz. An active bank account in the student's own name is required.
description:
The Vidyasamunnathi Diploma and Certificate Scholarship 2026-27 offers ₹6,000 to selected students from economically disadvantaged forward communities of Kerala. Applications close on 7 November 2026. Before starting the form, check that your course lasts at least one year and that your admission route meets the scheme's rules.

Does your course fit this category?

You must be taking a regular, full-time diploma or certificate course. The official diploma guidelines cover eligible government, aided and self-financing educational, research or scientific institutions in Kerala recognised by a university in the state.

For an institution outside Kerala, admission must have been obtained through a national-level competitive examination. Admission through an entrance test conducted by that institution itself does not qualify. Upload evidence of the national-level admission route with your application.

A course shorter than one year does not belong in this scholarship category. The guidelines direct such students towards coaching assistance instead. You cannot apply for both this scholarship and coaching assistance in the same category.

Marks, age and family income

  • You must belong to a non-reserved forward community of Kerala.

  • You need at least 60% marks or a B grade in SSLC or an equivalent examination.

  • Your annual family income from all sources must not exceed ₹4 lakh.

  • You must not have completed 25 years of age on the date applications are invited.

  • You need an active account in your own name at a nationalised or scheduled bank.

The guidelines exclude recipients of another central or state government scholarship or stipend, except e-grantz. The institution certificate also asks the signatory to confirm that the student receives no other scholarship or stipend apart from e-grantz. If you receive another form of financial assistance, clarify your position with Samunnathi before asking the institution to sign.

Get the institution certificate ready

Download the prescribed 2026-27 diploma certificate. It records your course, semester or year, regular full-time status and programme duration. The head of the institution or an authorised signatory must sign it and add the office seal, place and date.

Also prepare your SSLC or equivalent mark list, the first page of your SSLC certificate, accepted caste proof, the bank passbook first page and ration-card pages 1 and 2. Caste proof must be the Village Officer's caste certificate or the SSLC page carrying the caste entry.

The Village Officer's family-income certificate must be in the name of the applicant, parent or guardian included in the ration card containing the applicant's name. An individual-income certificate is not accepted. Check that your account number, IFSC and branch are readable and match the form.

Apply online and keep a copy

Use the official Samunnathi portal. Register and create a profile if you are a new applicant, or sign in with your existing login. Complete a fresh application for 2026-27, attach the required scans and submit before the deadline. Previous applications do not carry forward.

The guidelines list 588 awards, subject to available funding, and prioritise lower-income applicants. Eligibility does not guarantee selection. Retain your submitted application; the guidelines do not require application and document copies to be posted to the corporation. For clarification, call 0471-2311215 or 6238170312.

Diploma scholarship FAQs

Can a six-month certificate student apply here?

No. This category requires a course lasting at least one year. Check the separate coaching-assistance rules for a shorter course.

Is an institution's own entrance exam enough for study outside Kerala?

No. The guidelines require admission through a national-level competitive examination and evidence of that admission route.

Does receiving e-grantz make me ineligible?

No. E-grantz is expressly excepted from the restriction on other government scholarships or stipends. You must still meet all the remaining conditions.

Can I reuse last year's application?

You may reuse your portal login, but you must submit a new scholarship application for the current academic year.

Students on degree courses can review the separate Vidyasamunnathi graduation scholarship. Browse the scholarship directory if your course falls outside this category.

title: Post-Matric Scholarship for Students with Disabilities 2026-27: Eligibility and NSP Deadline
provider: Department of Empowerment of Persons with Disabilities, Government of India
amount: Fee reimbursement, maintenance and book allowances
eligibility: Indian students with a benchmark disability of at least 40% who are studying a recognised course from Class 11 through postgraduate degree or diploma may be eligible. The 2024 government guidelines set a parental income ceiling of ₹2.5 lakh a year. A valid disability certificate and UDID or UDID enrolment are required.
description:
Students with benchmark disabilities pursuing recognised study after Class 10 can check the Post-Matric Scholarship for Students with Disabilities on the National Scholarship Portal (NSP). The portal lists 31 October 2026 as the student application deadline for the 2026-27 academic year. This page was prepared by DekhoCampus on 23 October 2026 using the current NSP scheme listing and the Department of Empowerment of Persons with Disabilities guidelines.

Who should check eligibility?

The scheme covers recognised post-matric courses from Class 11 to a postgraduate degree or diploma. Applicants must be Indian nationals with a benchmark disability of at least 40%. The government guidelines require a valid disability certificate, UDID or UDID enrolment, and parental income not exceeding ₹2.5 lakh per year. A student repeating a class cannot receive this scholarship for that class a second time.

What support does it offer?

The 2024 guidelines set different limits for fees and allowances. Actual fee reimbursement cannot exceed the payable amount. The figures below are scheme limits, not a promise that every applicant will receive each component.

Component

Guideline amount

Admission and tuition fees

Up to ₹1.40 lakh per year, subject to actual fees

Other compulsory fees

Up to ₹10,000 per year, subject to actual fees

Maintenance

₹1,200 per month for hostellers or ₹650 for day scholars

Books

₹1,500 per year

Disability allowances also apply: ₹4,000 a year for visual impairment or intellectual disabilities, and ₹2,000 for other disability types, according to the official guidelines. Awards are subject to verification and available slots.

How to proceed

Open the NSP scheme list, confirm the post-matric entry and use the portal’s student application route. Keep the disability certificate, UDID details, income proof, course records and bank information ready. The NSP announcement says students with disabilities must first give consent to share UDID details through the UDID portal before submitting the NSP application. The related AICTE Swanath scholarship guide covers a different support route for eligible technical students.

Common questions

Is the scheme only for college students?

No. The post-matric component begins at Class 11 and extends through eligible postgraduate courses.

Does meeting the criteria guarantee an award?

No. The government guidelines provide a fixed number of slots and require application verification. Check your status on NSP after submitting.

title: Sage IT India Scholarship 2026: ₹50,000 Award and 15 November Deadline
amount: ₹50,000 one-time award
eligibility: Students aged 17-30 enrolled at a recognised college or university in India may enter individually. All disciplines and degree levels are welcome. The entry must be unpublished.
description:
What to prepare for your entry

The required topic is “Designing your role in an AI-First world: What will you choose to be responsible for?” Write 1,000-1,500 words and submit a Word .doc file. There is no entry fee.

Start with a situation you understand from your subject or intended career. For example, consider how a draft generated by software reaches a person who must approve it. Then explain the judgement that person still needs. A narrow, well-explained example is easier to develop than a list of predictions about every industry.

Send the article to Sage IT

Email the attachment to scholarships@sageitinc.com. Use the filename Topic_FirstName_LastName_UniversityName. Include your name, email, birth date, postal address, city, state, institution and area of study in the message.

Open the attachment once before sending it. Check that the version attached is your final draft, the filename identifies you correctly and the message contains the requested details. Keep the sent email and a copy of the file together so you can refer to exactly what you submitted.

Budget around a competitive award

The winner is scheduled to be announced on 30 November 2026. The ₹50,000 payment goes to the winner’s college or university, rather than their personal account.

Keep your regular fee-payment plan in place while awaiting the result. You can also compare other scholarship opportunities whose eligibility fits your course and circumstances.

Questions about the Sage IT scholarship

Is it only for computer science students?

No. Students from other disciplines can enter.

Can two students send a joint article?

No. Submit an individual entry.

What should I check immediately before emailing?

Review the current official instructions, your word count, attachment and contact details. A useful final check is to read the email as if you were receiving it: can the reader identify you and open the correct article without guessing?

title: Pratiksha Trust Scholarship 2026-27: Kerala Eligibility and 10 December Deadline
amount: Up to ₹54,000 a year for Engineering; ₹60,000 for MBBS
eligibility: For first-year Engineering or MBBS students from Kerala with annual family income below ₹3 lakh and a good relevant entrance rank. Read the current rules before applying, especially the Plus Two marks requirement and restriction on receiving another scholarship.
description:
Pratiksha Trust’s Anandam Senapathy Scholarship is accepting applications for 2026-27 until 10 December 2026. If you are starting Engineering or MBBS and need help with study costs, check the Kerala and income conditions before registering. The award is not available simply because you have secured a college seat.

Budget for the course-specific ceiling

The official application page lists annual support of up to ₹54,000 for Engineering and ₹60,000 for MBBS. These are maximum amounts, not guaranteed payments to every applicant. Keep a separate plan for costs that remain after any award.

The Trust’s programme is also called the Anandam Senapathy Scholarship. Use the official programme name when discussing it with your college, so that it is not confused with a different organisation bearing a similar name.

Resolve eligibility before filling the form

The 2026-27 rules require Plus Two completion in Kerala, admission in the current academic year, family income below ₹3 lakh and a good KEAM, JEE or NEET score. NEET applicants must give their All-India Rank. Students already receiving another scholarship are excluded.

If your Plus Two score is exactly 80%, seek clarification from the Trust first. Its application page says at least 80%, but the linked rules require above 80%. Do not assume eligibility from the shorter summary. Read the 2026-27 rules PDF alongside the official application guidance.

Prepare clear records before registering

Required uploads are a photograph, admission receipt, Plus Two marksheet, entrance rank sheet and income certificate. Check that names, course details and figures agree across your records. Use legible scans and review each attachment before submitting.

Start from the Trust’s official application page and follow its Registration Open link. Keep your login details private. Review the completed form yourself and retain any acknowledgement the portal provides.

What happens after the application?

The Trust’s selection process considers merit, financial circumstances, application completeness, extracurricular activities and support needs. Shortlisting leads to an interview and verification; its process page also describes a house visit. Submission alone does not mean selection.

Annual continuation depends on satisfactory academic performance, updated supporting documents and continued sponsorship. Treat renewal as a condition to meet each year, not an automatic promise for the whole degree.

When comparing other options in the scholarship directory, check whether awards can be combined before accepting them.

Application questions

Is ₹60,000 the award for Engineering students too?

No. The advertised Engineering ceiling is ₹54,000 per year; ₹60,000 is the MBBS ceiling.

Does registration mean I have been selected?

No. The Trust shortlists applicants, interviews them and verifies their details before final selection.

Where should I begin the application?

Use the Registration Open link on Pratiksha Trust’s official application page. The published deadline is 10 December 2026.
