title: Vidyadhan Mathura Scholarship for Women in STEM 2026: Apply by 31 October
eligibility: For women admitted to the first year of a STEM or healthcare degree in 2026-27. Applicants need at least 70% in Class XII (60% for students with disabilities), annual family income below ₹3 lakh, and a Mathura connection: Class XII schooling in the district or current study at an institution there. Check the official Vidyadhan programme before applying.
description:
Who can apply

This is for women beginning a first-year STEM or healthcare degree in the 2026-27 academic year. Vidyadhan names engineering, Bachelor of Science and medicine among its examples. Applicants must score at least 70% in Class XII, or 60% if they have a disability, and have annual family income under ₹3 lakh. They must have either finished Class XII at a school in Mathura District or now study at an institution there. Admission to the first year must already be secured.

Funding and selection

The award is ₹15,000-₹75,000 per year, varying by course, and may continue until course completion if academic performance remains satisfactory. It also includes training and mentoring. An eligible application is not an award: Vidyadhan lists a test and interview before final selection. Interviews are planned for 15-30 November 2026; exact appointments will be sent to shortlisted applicants.

Apply without missing a document

Vidyadhan lists 31 October 2026 as the last application date. On the official scholarship portal, open the Mathura women-in-STEM programme, create your own account and complete the form. Use an email address you regularly check: activation and later updates arrive there. Upload a photograph, Class XII marksheet, Class X marksheet and income certificate from a competent authority. A ration card will not substitute for the certificate. The foundation says application is free and is complete only after mandatory files are uploaded.

Do not confuse the programmes

The portal shows many general Vidyadhan state programmes as closed. The Mathura women-in-STEM degree programme is separately marked open. Check the programme name before applying rather than assuming the closed Uttar Pradesh Class XI listing covers this opportunity. You can compare other current options in the DekhoCampus scholarship directory.

title: Muthoot M George Scholarship 2026-27: Kerala Applications Close 31 October
amount: an award subject to the foundation’s terms (amount not announced)
eligibility: For permanent residents of Kerala entering the first year of MBBS, BTech or BSc Nursing in 2026-27, including eligible students studying outside Kerala. The official form requires at least 90% or equivalent in Plus Two, annual family income not exceeding ₹2 lakh, qualification in the relevant entrance examination and admission to a recognised institution.
description:
Who can apply for the Kerala edition?

The Muthoot M George Foundation, the CSR arm of The Muthoot Group, runs this higher education scholarship. Its official page identifies 2026-27 as the 10th edition and announces 30 scholarships for Kerala students in MBBS, BTech and BSc Nursing.

The linked application is for first-year students who are permanent residents of Kerala. Your college may be outside the state. The academic threshold is 90% or equivalent in Plus Two, and annual family income must not exceed ₹2 lakh. Applicants must have qualified in the relevant entrance examination and obtained admission to a recognised institution.

The form says a student below 90% may submit an application but may not qualify. This does not remove the stated marks requirement. It also says applicants above the income ceiling cannot submit.

What support is confirmed?

The foundation describes scholarships covering the course duration, subject to its terms and conditions. A fixed amount for the current Kerala round is not specified on the official page or application introduction. Selection and financial support are not guaranteed by submitting the form.

Prepare these documents before applying

  • Applicant’s Aadhaar, parent or guardian’s Aadhaar, and the signed parent or guardian consent form.

  • A passport photograph and a self-request letter in English.

  • Plus One and Plus Two marksheets, along with the entrance rank or scorecard.

  • An income certificate, bonafide certificate, proof of college admission and admission allotment memo.

  • A recommendation letter.

The self-request letter, bonafide certificate and recommendation letter must be addressed to the Managing Director, Muthoot Finance Limited, Kochi. The application accepts PDF, JPG and PNG uploads up to 10 MB per file. Use clear, complete scans so that names, marks and issuing details remain readable.

Submit through the foundation’s application link

title: Vidyasamunnathi National Institute Scholarship 2026-27: Fee Reimbursement up to ₹50,000
provider: Kerala State Welfare Corporation for Forward Communities
amount: Up to ₹50,000 in eligible fee reimbursement
eligibility:
For students from non-reserved forward communities of Kerala taking a regular, full-time course at a premier national institution covered by the scheme. Annual family income must not exceed ₹4 lakh. Applicants must be under 35 on the date applications are invited and have an active bank account in their own name.

Students receiving another central or state government scholarship or stipend are not eligible under these category-specific guidelines. Check your institution and funding status before applying.
description:
The Vidyasamunnathi National Institute Scholarship 2026-27 can reimburse eligible study fees up to ₹50,000 for selected students. The online application deadline is 7 November 2026. Keep your original fee receipts safe: this category has a document-submission step after selection.


Which fees can be reimbursed?

The official national-institute guidelines cover course or tuition fees, examination fees and hostel fees paid for the academic year. Mess charges are excluded. The ₹50,000 figure is a ceiling on eligible reimbursement, not a flat payment to every applicant.

The guidelines list 54 scholarships, with the number linked to available funding. Lower-income applicants receive priority. Ask your institution to certify the actual amounts paid in each eligible fee category.


Check your institution and personal eligibility

You must belong to a non-reserved forward community of Kerala and study on a regular, full-time course at a covered premier national institution. The guidelines give examples including IITs, IIMs, NITs, IISc, JIPMER, National Law Schools, National Film Schools and NIFT. If your institution is not clearly covered, confirm with Samunnathi before applying.

  • Annual family income from all sources must not exceed ₹4 lakh.

  • You must be under 35 on the date applications are invited. The rule is not based on your age on the submission deadline.

  • You need an active account in your own name at a nationalised or scheduled bank.

  • Recipients of another central or state government scholarship or stipend are not eligible under this category’s guidelines.


Get the fee certificate before submitting

Download the 2026-27 institution certificate. It has separate entries for tuition, examination and hostel fees, with mess charges excluded. The head of the institution or authorised signatory must sign it, provide a phone number and add the office seal.

Prepare readable scans of that certificate, the Village Officer’s family-income certificate, accepted caste proof, the bank passbook first page, ration card pages 1 and 2, and your SSLC certificate. Caste proof must be the Village Officer’s caste certificate or the SSLC page containing the caste entry.

The family-income certificate must be in the name of the applicant, parent or guardian listed on the ration card containing the applicant’s name. An individual-income certificate is not accepted. Check the account number, IFSC and branch before uploading the passbook scan.


Apply online, then watch for the selection message

Use the official Samunnathi portal. New users register and create a profile; existing users can reuse their login. Submit a fresh scholarship application for 2026-27, even if you received support previously. Upload the documents and retain a copy of the completed form.

Selected applicants are contacted by SMS or email. The guidelines then require the application copy, original fee receipts and other required documents to be sent within the notified time limit to Kerala State Welfare Corporation for Forward Communities Ltd, L2, Kuleena, Jawahar Nagar, Kowdiar P.O., Thiruvananthapuram.

Mark the envelope “Application for Vidyasamunnathi Scheme (2026-27)”. Follow the deadline in the selection communication for this later step; the 7 November date is the online application deadline. For clarification, contact Samunnathi on 0471-2311215 or 6238170312.


National-institute scholarship FAQs

Is ₹50,000 guaranteed if I am eligible?

No. Reimbursement depends on eligible fees, the institution certificate, original receipts, selection and funding. ₹50,000 is the maximum for an academic year.

Can I include hostel mess charges?

No. The guidelines and certificate explicitly exclude mess charges from the hostel-fee amount.

Do I send original receipts before applying online?

The process begins online. Selected applicants receive an SMS or email and must then send the application copy, original receipts and required documents within the notified time limit.

Can I renew last year’s award automatically?

No. Submit a fresh application for 2026-27. An existing portal account can be reused, but the previous application does not carry forward.

PhD scholars can also review the separate Vidyasamunnathi research scholarship, which has its own eligibility and funding restrictions. Browse the scholarship directory to compare relevant options before choosing a category.

title: APJ Abdul Kalam Scholarship Kerala 2026-27: ₹6,000 and Application Dates
provider: Directorate of Minority Welfare, Government of Kerala
amount: ₹6,000 for 2026-27; awarded only once
eligibility:
Permanent residents of Kerala from Muslim, Christian, Sikh, Buddhist, Jain or Parsi communities can apply if admitted on a merit seat to a three-year diploma at a government, aided or government-recognised self-financing polytechnic in Kerala. Second- and third-year students are also eligible for consideration.

BPL applicants receive preference. If BPL applicants are unavailable, APL applicants with annual family income up to ₹8 lakh may be considered. Previous recipients must not apply again.
description:
Check the admission route before applying

The scholarship covers merit-seat admissions. If you study at a self-financing polytechnic, check both its government recognition and the seat category shown in your allotment memo. Studying a diploma course by itself does not establish eligibility.

The department selects minority-community students using family income and marks, in proportion to population. Women have a 30% reservation; unfilled places in that quota may be given to men. Meeting the eligibility conditions does not guarantee selection.

Four dates to keep with your application

  • 25 November 2026: students must finish the online application.

  • 28 November 2026: submit the registration printout and supporting documents to the head of your institution.

  • 30 November 2026: the institution must complete scrutiny and online approval.

  • 5 December 2026: heads of self-financing polytechnics must forward approved applications to the Directorate of Minority Welfare.

The last two dates are institutional steps. Ask your college how it will confirm receipt of your documents and whether anything needs correcting before approval.

Register, upload and hand over your documents

Use the Minority Welfare scholarship portal. New applicants start with one-time registration using their basic details, Aadhaar and phone number. After logging in, complete the personal, bank and current institution sections, add previous qualifications, and choose APJ Abdul Kalam Scholarship under Apply For Scholarship.

The online instructions require a photograph, signature, SSLC certificate, income certificate, bank passbook and allotment memo. The document checklist also includes the application printout, relevant Plus Two or VHSE marksheets, Aadhaar, community or minority certificate, ration card and an authenticated Village Office income certificate.

Use a bank account in your own name. The passbook copy must show the account number, IFSC and branch details. Compare these with the form before submission: the guidelines warn that incorrect bank information can lead to rejection.

After submitting, use the portal’s Submitted Applications section to follow progress. Give the printed application and supporting copies to your institution within the student handover deadline. Government and aided institutions retain approved applications; self-financing polytechnics have an additional forwarding step to the Directorate at Vikas Bhavan, Thiruvananthapuram.

Questions diploma students may have

Can I apply in the second or third year?

Yes. Those years are considered too, provided you meet the other rules and have not already received this scholarship.

Is ₹6,000 paid every year?

The current guidelines specify ₹6,000 for the academic year and state that the scholarship is granted only once. Do not budget for an automatic annual renewal.

Can a self-financing polytechnic student apply?

Yes, if the institution is government-recognised and the admission is on a merit seat. Your college must also complete the additional forwarding requirement.

Is online submission enough?

No. The printout and documents must reach your institution by 28 November 2026, followed by institutional verification and approval.

For other course-specific support, compare the DekhoCampus scholarship listings and check each scheme’s separate conditions.

title: Thakur Sen Negi Scholarship 2026-27: HPBOSE Merit and NSP Deadline
provider: Himachal Pradesh Department of Higher Education
amount: ₹11,000 per year for up to two years after Class 10
eligibility: ST students of Himachal Pradesh selected among the top 100 girls and top 100 boys in HPBOSE matric results, continuing in Classes 11 and 12 or a recognised post-matric professional or technical course. Institutions may be within or outside the state; renewal requires satisfactory academic progress.
description:
If you're an ST student from Himachal Pradesh continuing after Class 10, check your HPBOSE merit position before applying for the Thakur Sen Negi Utkrisht Chatravriti Yojana. The scheme selects the top 100 girls and top 100 boys from the state's tribal community. Passing Class 10 alone doesn't secure the award.

For 2026-27, the National Scholarship Portal's Himachal Pradesh scheme listing gives 31 October 2026 as the student application deadline. Look for the scheme's full name under State Schemes and Himachal Pradesh, then use the NSP student application route.

HPBOSE merit is the starting point

The Himachal Pradesh government's scheme guidelines linked by NSP base selection on the matric examination conducted by the Himachal Pradesh Board of School Education, Dharamshala. Applicants must belong to a Scheduled Tribe of Himachal Pradesh recognised by the state government.

The next course matters too. Selected students can study in Classes 11 and 12 at a recognised institution, or take a recognised professional or technical course after matric. The institution may be within or outside Himachal Pradesh. If you passed Class 10 through another board, don't assume the HPBOSE-based selection rule covers you: ask the scholarship office to confirm before relying on this award.

Two years of support, not the whole course

The award is ₹11,000 per eligible student per year for two successive years after matric. For a professional or technical course, support is also limited to a maximum of two years, even when the course itself lasts longer.

Renewal is conditional. Class 12 support depends on satisfactory performance in the Class 11 internal examination. For a professional or technical course, second-year renewal depends on satisfactory first-year performance. Keep the relevant result ready rather than assuming that the first payment guarantees the next one.

Submit before the student window closes

NSP separates application submission from verification. Students must apply by 31 October 2026; defective-application and institute verification remain open until 17 November, followed by DNO/SNO/MNO verification until 18 November. Those later dates are not extra days to start a fresh student application.

  1. Ask your school's scholarship office how to confirm your place in the relevant HPBOSE merit group.

  2. Keep your matric marksheet, ST certificate and current admission details ready. Follow the document requirements shown for your profile.

  3. Use the official NSP student portal to complete and submit the application. Save its reference and acknowledgement.

  4. Track the status and respond if the institution asks you to correct a defect. Contact the scholarship office promptly if the scheme or your institution is missing from the application options.

For girls planning further study after Class 12, the Kalpana Chawla scholarship's post-Plus-Two merit rules cover a different stage of education. It isn't an alternative way to qualify for this Class 10-based award.

Frequently asked questions

Does every ST student who passes Class 10 qualify?

No. Selection is limited to the top 100 girls and top 100 boys from Himachal Pradesh's tribal community in the HPBOSE matric results, subject to the scheme's study conditions.

Can I study outside Himachal Pradesh?

Yes. The guidelines allow a recognised institution within or outside the state. The Himachal Pradesh ST and HPBOSE merit conditions still apply.

Will a three-year diploma receive three years of funding?

No. The scheme limits professional or technical course support to two years after matric, with satisfactory progress required for second-year renewal.

Can I wait until the November verification deadline to apply?

No. The current NSP student deadline is 31 October 2026. November dates are for verification, not an extension of the student application window.

Who can apply?

The scheme covers permanent residents of Odisha in the Scheduled Tribe, Scheduled Caste, OBC/SEBC and economically backward class (EBC) categories. You must be on a recognised post-matric course at a government, aided or private institution recognised by the competent authority. The parent or guardian’s income from all sources must not exceed ₹2.5 lakh a year. OBC/SEBC and EBC applicants need at least 50% in the last qualifying examination. These are the conditions shown in the official scheme details; check the category shown against your documents before you apply.

Studying outside Odisha does not automatically rule out an Odisha resident. The portal lists an institute declaration certificate for out-of-state applicants. It also says correspondence and online courses qualify only when offered by a central or state university. A second course at the same level in another subject, such as a Bachelor of Commerce degree after a Bachelor of Arts degree, is not covered under its stated conditions.

How much will you receive?

There is no universal award amount. The official portal describes course-fee support and an annual academic or maintenance allowance by category and course grouping, subject to the relevant guidelines. Check your own course group and the fee rules in the scheme listing before budgeting. A headline figure from another course may not be your entitlement. Payment goes to the student’s Aadhaar-seeded bank account.

Apply through the Odisha portal

Use the Odisha State Scholarship Portal to check eligibility, register or sign in, choose the department and scheme, complete the student, academic and bank details, then submit and download the form. Its application guide explains each stage. Keep the mobile number linked to your Aadhaar active so you can receive the registration OTP.

Documents worth preparing first

Have your category certificate or EBC self-declaration, income certificate, Aadhaar, bank-passbook page, photograph and academic records ready. Depending on your situation, the portal also asks for a disability certificate, hostel certificate or an institute declaration for study outside Odisha. If your institution or course is missing from the dropdown, ask the institute to contact its District Welfare Officer rather than selecting a different course.

Review the application carefully before final submission. The portal says you can edit most entries until you submit; if you find an error afterwards, your institute can revert the form for correction. For students in Classes 11 and 12, Odisha also lists the separate Junior Merit Scholarship and Pathani Samanta mathematics award. Those have their own eligibility checks and should not be treated as part of this post-matric application.

Questions applicants often ask

Can an Odisha resident studying in another state apply?

The official scheme details include an institute declaration certificate for out-of-state applicants. Check that your institution and course meet the recognition rules before submitting.

Does every applicant need 50% marks?

The 50% condition in the portal is specifically stated for OBC/SEBC and EBC applicants. Use the official category rules for your own application.

Is the award a fixed amount?

No. Course-fee and allowance rules vary by category and course group. The portal directs applicants to the scheme guidelines for the applicable amount.

title: Mary Gates Research Scholarship 2026: Funding for UW Undergraduates
provider: Mary Gates Endowment, University of Washington
amount: up to USD 5,000 across two quarters
eligibility: Applicants must be enrolled in a bachelor’s degree at the University of Washington’s Seattle, Bothell or Tacoma campus and plan research with a UW-affiliated faculty mentor. International students are eligible. All majors and undergraduate years are welcome; full-time enrolment is required during funded quarters.
description:
Already studying for a bachelor’s degree at the University of Washington? The Mary Gates Research Scholarship can help fund your research, including work outside science and engineering. Indian students enrolled at UW are eligible as international students. But this is not an admission offer or a scholarship for someone studying at an Indian college.

Make sure your project and enrolment fit

The Endowment’s research eligibility rules cover UW’s Seattle, Bothell and Tacoma campuses. You can apply from any undergraduate year or major, including while your project is still being planned. The research must have support from a UW-affiliated faculty mentor.

Full-time enrolment is required during the quarters when you receive funding, rather than necessarily during the Autumn application quarter. If your graduation or course-load plans might change, resolve that with the programme before choosing your funded quarters.

Two deadlines, not one

The current Research Scholarship notice gives 26 October 2026 as the application deadline and 28 October 2026 as the recommendation-letter deadline. Both are listed at 5 p.m. The notice does not label the time zone. If you are submitting from India, confirm it with the Mary Gates programme team rather than assuming Indian Standard Time.

Your submission alone does not complete the application: UW also needs the mentor’s letter. The request normally goes to your mentor after you submit, although the portal lets you send it earlier. Speak to the mentor first, then leave enough time for them to respond.

Prepare the writing before opening the form

UW’s application instructions distinguish three pieces of writing. Use the short summary to explain the project plainly; save the methods and reasoning for the essay.

Application component

Official length or format

What to focus on

Project summary

50 words

The question and work you plan to undertake

Project essay

Three-page PDF

Research purpose, methods, contribution and mentorship

Impact response

One-page PDF

How the research and funding relate to your education and future plans

The essay should be double-spaced in 12-point type with one-inch margins. UW allows an optional extra page for references, images or figures; in-text citations still count within the three-page essay. Don’t turn that extra page into more essay text.

Use the official Research Scholarship application and sign in with your UW NetID. The form asks permission to release your transcript. Its instructions do not ask you to upload that transcript. Enter your mentor’s details carefully and review each completed section before submitting.

How much funding should you plan around?

The university’s Autumn 2026 announcement describes USD 5,000 paid as USD 2,500 per quarter over two quarters. UW’s application guidance also warns that financial aid can affect the amount received, and the maximum across Mary Gates awards in a quarter is USD 2,500. Treat the award as competitive support, not guaranteed income.

If you are not enrolled at UW, this application is not the right route. Compare scholarships with different enrolment requirements instead of spending time on a form you cannot qualify for.

Questions applicants often miss

Can I apply before my research has started?

Yes. UW welcomes projects still in the planning stage. You still need to explain the intended research and arrange the faculty mentorship and recommendation required by the application.

Can a postgraduate researcher be my primary mentor?

The primary mentor must be a UW-affiliated faculty member. A graduate student or postdoctoral researcher can be an optional secondary mentor, not a replacement for the faculty mentor.

Does submitting by 26 October finish the process?

No. The mentor’s letter must also reach UW by its separate 28 October deadline. Keep track of both parts; a submitted student form without the letter is incomplete.

title: Science Ambassador Scholarship 2027: $20,000 Awards for US STEM Study
amount: US$20,000 once for each of five winners
eligibility: Women and non-binary high school seniors or undergraduate students pursuing a STEM major. US citizenship is not required, but full-time college study in the United States during 2027-28 is required by the application form. Graduate students are ineligible.
level: Undergraduate STEM; high school seniors may apply
description:
Planning undergraduate STEM study in the United States? The Science Ambassador Scholarship is accepting applications for five US$20,000 awards. Indian citizenship does not exclude you, but the application requires full-time US college attendance during 2027-28. This is not funding for a degree studied entirely in India.

Check the study requirement first

Cards Against Humanity offers this award to women and non-binary students. High school seniors and current undergraduates can apply; postgraduate students cannot. STEM must be your major. If you have not declared one, you must commit to STEM throughout your undergraduate study. Read the official eligibility and award terms before recording.

Each award is a one-time tuition contribution, not a promise to cover your whole degree. Include remaining tuition and living expenses in your college budget.

Teach one idea in three minutes

Choose a STEM idea you can explain clearly. The video should teach the audience, rather than describe why you deserve funding. It can cover a topic outside your intended major. Keep it within three minutes, check the science and cite your sources. Expensive production is unnecessary.

Upload a public YouTube video, not a Short. A landscape format such as 16:9 helps avoid automatic conversion to a Short. Test the exact video link while signed out, so a privacy setting does not prevent the reviewers from watching.

Confirm the application, not just the upload

The deadline is 14 December 2026 at 11:59 pm US Central Time. Leave time for uploading and confirmation rather than treating midnight in India as the cutoff.

  1. Open the official application form.

  2. Enter your school, intended STEM field and public video link, then check the eligibility declarations.

  3. Submit and use the confirmation email to confirm your entry. Unconfirmed videos are not reviewed.

  4. Keep that email: its link allows edits until the deadline.

The initial form asks for the video link and school details; it does not list income-proof uploads.

Compare other funding routes in the scholarship directory, especially if your planned university is outside the US.

Application questions

Can I apply from India?

Yes, if you meet the eligibility conditions and will study full time in the US during 2027-28. Citizenship alone is not the deciding condition.

Does a YouTube upload complete the application?

No. Submit its public link through the official form and confirm the entry using the email you receive.

Can I fix a submitted application?

Yes. Use the link in your confirmation email before the deadline.

title: Ishan Uday Scholarship 2026-27: ₹80,000 a Year for Northeast Students
amount: ₹8,000 per month for 10 months (₹80,000 a year)
eligibility: For students with a valid North Eastern Region domicile certificate who passed Class 12 from a school in the region and have joined the first year of their first recognised undergraduate degree. Study must be regular and full-time at an eligible institution in India. Parents’ annual income must be below ₹4.5 lakh. Management-quota admissions and open, distance, correspondence, private or part-time study are excluded.
description:
Check both your school background and college admission

Ishan Uday supports a first undergraduate degree. You must already be in its first year when you apply; an admission offer without enrolment is not enough. You also need a valid domicile certificate from a North Eastern state and a Class 12 qualification from a school within that region through a recognised board, including CBSE, ICSE or NIOS.

The college itself may be anywhere in India. Under the official UGC scheme guidelines, eligible institutions include UGC-listed institutions under Section 2(f), deemed universities under Section 3, qualifying institutions fully funded by central or state governments, and Institutions of National Importance. The applicable NAAC accreditation condition takes effect from 2025-26. A valid AISHE code is required for the institution to use NSP, but the code alone does not establish every aspect of eligibility. Ask your nodal officer to confirm your institution’s category.

Parents’ income must be below ₹4.5 lakh a year. An income of exactly ₹4.5 lakh does not qualify. A second undergraduate degree, management-quota admission, or study through an excluded mode will also make a fresh application ineligible.

What the award covers and how selection works

The scholarship pays ₹8,000 per month for 10 months, which totals ₹80,000 for an academic year. UGC provides 10,000 scholarships annually. Half the slots in each category are earmarked for arts, humanities, social sciences, law and management; the other half cover science, engineering and technology, medicine, technical courses, agriculture and forestry.

Selection follows state-wise merit among applicants. Where Class 12 marks are tied at the merit-list cutoff, Class 10 marks are considered next, followed by age, with older candidates preferred. Treat the award as competitive funding rather than money guaranteed by registration.

Payment goes to the selected student’s Aadhaar-linked bank account through direct benefit transfer. Check that your name, account number and IFSC match your records before submitting. For integrated or dual-degree courses, support is limited to the undergraduate component.

Application and verification deadlines are different

The NSP scheme list, under UGC, gives these dates for 2026-27:

Stage

Date

What to do

Student application

31 October 2026

Complete and submit the application before this deadline.

Defective application and institute verification

15 November 2026

Track the application and follow up with your institution on any flagged issue.

District, state and ministry nodal verification

30 November 2026

Continue checking status after institute verification.

The student application window opened on 16 September 2026. Do not wait for a verification date to submit a fresh form. The UGC FAQ says students cannot edit an application after the closing date.

Submit on NSP, then stay in touch with your college

  1. Open the official NSP student portal and follow its registration or sign-in process.

  2. Check that your profile, college and course details are correct before selecting Ishan Uday.

  3. Keep your domicile, parents’ income, Class 12 marks and admission records ready for your institution. Supply any additional evidence it requests under the scheme.

  4. Review the complete application, submit it before 31 October and retain the acknowledgement.

  5. Check the status and contact the scholarship nodal officer if institutional verification remains pending.

The guidelines place document checking with the institution. Follow the current portal’s instructions rather than sending certificates to an unofficial application service. Incomplete or unverified applications are not considered for an award.

Plan for renewal before changing your course

Continuing support requires successful progression, prescribed attendance and good conduct, with a renewal application on NSP each year. Changing the course or institution forfeits the scholarship under the published rules. Check the implications with your nodal officer before making either change.

You can receive only one scholarship or monetary benefit at a time under these rules. Declare existing support when applying. If selected, you must choose which benefit to retain.

Questions Northeast applicants often ask

Can I apply if I study outside the Northeast?

Yes. An eligible college elsewhere in India is allowed. You must still meet the Northeast domicile and Class 12 schooling conditions, along with the other scheme rules.

Does submitting the form mean I will receive ₹80,000?

No. Your application must be verified and you must be selected through the merit process. ₹80,000 is the annual amount calculated from 10 monthly payments, not a guaranteed payment to every applicant.

Is Ishan Uday available for a master’s degree?

No. It supports a first undergraduate degree, including only the UG part of an integrated course. For postgraduate study, see the separate UGC postgraduate scholarship and check its own eligibility rules.

Where should I check official answers and application status?

Use the UGC Ishan Uday FAQ for scheme questions and your NSP account for application status. Your institution’s scholarship nodal officer handles college-level verification queries.

title: Puducherry Retention Scholarship 2026-27: Support for Primary-School Girls
provider: Adi Dravidar Welfare and Scheduled Tribes Welfare Department, Puducherry
amount: ₹500 per month for 10 months under the amended rules
eligibility:
For SC girls studying in Classes 1-5 in a government or government-recognised private school in Puducherry. The base rules require Puducherry nativity or at least five years of continuous residence, supported by the relevant certificate.

Check the current income-document requirements with the school before applying. Older forms show income ceilings, while a March 2025 government notification records that the limit for educational schemes was removed in 2009. Do not rule out an application using an old threshold alone.
description:
Check the school and residence requirements first

The retention scheme rules linked by NSP cover SC girls in Classes 1-5 at government and recognised private schools in the Union Territory. They allow Puducherry natives or students with at least five years of continuous residence. The relevant nativity or residence certificate must come from the competent revenue authority.

The department’s current service list and the 2025 amendment also refer to SC/ST girls, while the NSP entry is labelled for SC girls. ST families should ask the school or department to confirm the applicable portal route before selecting a category.

Use the amended scholarship rate

G.O. Ms. No. 06/2025/ADW&STW, dated 1 April 2025, replaces ₹100 with ₹500 in Rule 5 and takes effect from 2025-26. Read it together with the base rule’s ten-month period. At that rate, ten months of support totals ₹5,000; the sanctioned payment depends on eligibility and approval.

Do not reject an application using an old income limit

The March 2025 Puducherry Gazette notification records that the income limit for educational schemes was removed in 2009. Its new ₹8 lakh ceiling concerns eight listed socio-economic welfare schemes; it should not be treated as a new retention-scholarship limit.

If an older form asks for an income certificate or quotes a different ceiling, show it to the school’s scholarship coordinator and ask which current instruction applies. Keep any certificate requested by the current form ready, without assuming that an old figure settles eligibility.

Apply through NSP and stay in touch with the school

  1. Open the NSP student section and follow its registration and application instructions.

  2. Check the 2026-27 scheme listing under UT of Puducherry. Select the retention scholarship entry for SC girl students.

  3. Confirm the child’s name, class, school and category details before submission. Use the documents requested by the current form.

  4. Submit by 31 October 2026 and save the application reference. Ask the school to check the application and monitor any correction request.

NSP lists defective-application and institute verification until 15 November, followed by department-level verification until 15 December. Those are verification stages, not extensions of the student application deadline.

The department’s online services page directs retention-scholarship applicants to NSP. For support at other study levels, browse scholarships on DekhoCampus; do not use a college scholarship form for a primary-school child.

Frequently asked questions

Can a Class 6 student apply for this retention scholarship?

The retention scheme described here covers Classes 1-5. A Class 6 student needs to check the separate scheme for her class rather than select this one.

Is the scholarship still ₹1,000 a year?

The April 2025 amendment sets the rate at ₹500 per month from 2025-26. The base rule provides ten months of support. Use the amendment with the underlying rules, rather than relying only on an older leaflet.

Does institute verification until 15 November extend the application deadline?

No. NSP lists 31 October 2026 as the student application deadline. The later date is for verification of applications.

What should a parent do if the form shows an old income ceiling?

Ask the school or the Adi Dravidar Welfare and Scheduled Tribes Welfare Department to confirm the current requirement before ruling out the application. The 2025 Gazette records the earlier removal of income limits for educational schemes.

title: Kalpana Chawla Chhatravriti Yojana 2026-27: HPBOSE Merit and NSP Deadline
provider: Himachal Pradesh Department of Higher Education
amount: ₹18,000 per year
eligibility: Bonafide Himachali girl students drawn from the HPBOSE Class 12 merit lists for Science, Arts and Commerce, who continue into an eligible regular course. The award is limited to the top 2,000 meritorious girls. Passing Class 12 alone does not secure a place.
description:
A Himachal Pradesh girl with strong Class 12 marks should check the HPBOSE merit position before counting on the Kalpana Chawla Chhatravriti Yojana. This is a limited state merit award, not a scholarship for every student who clears Plus Two. The Himachal Pradesh Directorate of Higher Education identifies the top 2,000 meritorious girls across Science, Arts and Commerce as the award group.

Where the merit list matters

The Directorate says HPBOSE supplies the post-Plus-Two merit lists, with places distributed by the passing ratio in each stream. That makes a general Class 12 pass certificate different from being in the scholarship's merit pool. If you are starting a degree, diploma or certificate course, ask your school or new institution's scholarship office how to confirm your merit-list position and whether your course is eligible. Do this before treating the scholarship as part of your fee plan.

Annual support and renewal

The state scheme description sets the award at ₹18,000 per student per year. It also says renewal can run until the degree, diploma or certificate course ends, provided the scholar does not fail. Renewal is therefore conditional; receiving the first payment does not guarantee support after an unsuccessful academic year.

Current application window

On the National Scholarship Portal, select State Schemes and Himachal Pradesh to find this scheme. NSP lists it as open for academic year 2026-27, with student applications closing on 31 October 2026. The student section is the official starting point; NSP requires a One Time Registration number for scholarship applications. Check the scheme shown in your account and your institution's details before submitting.

Have your HPBOSE Class 12 record, Himachali domicile details, current admission information and bank particulars ready to compare with the live form. The portal's prompts govern the actual documents required. If the scheme does not appear or the institution details are wrong, contact the scholarship office rather than choosing an unrelated award. You can also browse other scholarship options on DekhoCampus while resolving the issue.

Questions applicants ask

Does passing HPBOSE Class 12 make me eligible automatically?

No. The state restricts this award to the top 2,000 meritorious girls selected from HPBOSE's post-Plus-Two merit lists across the three streams. A pass alone is not confirmation of selection.

Can the ₹18,000 continue after the first year?

The state allows renewal through an eligible degree, diploma or certificate course, but says it ceases if the scholar fails. Confirm your renewal requirements with the institution each year.

Where should I check the application deadline?

Use the current NSP Himachal Pradesh scheme listing. It displays 31 October 2026 for student applications to this scheme, while later verification dates are for institutes and officials, not extra time for a student to apply.

description:

The Ministry of Home Affairs guidelines cover wards and widows of eligible Central Armed Police Forces and Assam Rifles personnel, including specified deceased, disabled, gallantry-award, retired and serving personnel categories. Check the exact category and supporting certificate in the official MHA guidelines before starting the form. Who meets the study requirement?

A new applicant must be pursuing a first professional degree in a recognised field covered by the scheme. The MHA guidelines list examples such as engineering, medicine, dental, veterinary, BBA, BCA, pharmacy, nursing, agriculture, MBA and MCA, subject to the detailed course conditions. The minimum entry qualification score is 60% for a fresh application. Renewal requires at least 50% in each subsequent academic year. Do not rely on the course name alone; check the guideline’s approved-course and institution rules.

The serving and retired personnel category in the guidelines is limited to personnel below officer rank. Other service categories have their own conditions. Keep the relevant service certificate and academic records ready, and confirm which applicant category your family fits.

Amount and selection

The MHA scheme states ₹3,000 a month for girls and ₹2,500 a month for boys. These are scholarship rates, not a promise that every eligible applicant will be selected. Use the National Scholarship Portal for the application. Check your entered name, qualifying marks, course and service-category documents before final submission, then retain the application acknowledgement.

Can a student in a general degree apply?

The scheme is for approved first professional degree programmes. Check the MHA course list and current NSP specifications before assuming a general degree qualifies.

Is 60% required for renewal too?

Can a CAPF applicant apply under the State Police scheme instead?

These are separate NSP listings with different service eligibility. Choose the scheme matching the personnel category shown on your documents.

title: Teach For India Fellowship 2027: Apply by 1 November for Paid Teaching
amount: ₹30,000 per month; relocation allowance where eligible
eligibility:
Applicants must be Indian citizens or Overseas Citizens of India (OCI), complete graduation by June or July 2027, and be applying for the first time to the 2027 cohort since July 2026.

Prior teaching experience is not required. Selected Fellows must commit to two years of full-time teaching and live in their placement city. Other professional or academic engagements are not permitted during the Fellowship.
description:
A paid fellowship built around classroom responsibility

Teach For India places Fellows in English-medium government or low-fee private schools serving underserved communities. The role lasts two years and involves teaching alongside work with school staff, families and other Fellows. It is a paid teaching and leadership programme, rather than a tuition grant for continuing an unrelated degree.

Placements are in Ahmedabad, Bengaluru, Chennai, Delhi, Gurugram, Hyderabad, Kolkata, Mumbai or Pune. Fellows must live in their placement city. Classes can range from grades 1 to 10; the teaching assignment may cover several subjects or specific subjects.

The application deadline and the graduation requirement

The official 2027 application portal gives the current deadline as 1 November 2026 at 11:59 PM IST. Submit before that time and retain the acknowledgement. The wider selection cycle mentioned in the FAQs should not be treated as an extension of this deadline.

You may apply before finishing your degree if you will graduate by June or July 2027. The other published requirements are Indian citizenship or OCI status and a first application to the 2027 cohort since July 2026. If you have already applied to this cohort, read the once-per-cycle rule before starting another form.

Understand the stipend and relocation support

The monthly stipend is ₹30,000. The official Fellowship FAQs also list a city compensatory allowance of ₹6,000 to ₹12,600 for Fellows relocating from their home city. The exact allowance depends on placement; it is not an identical extra payment for everyone.

The stipend applies during the Summer Institute as well. Relocating Fellows become eligible for the city allowance only after moving to their placement city. Other published benefits include work-related expense reimbursements, health insurance up to ₹1 lakh, counselling access and leave arrangements. Check the offer and programme terms for the details applicable to you.

Prepare examples, then complete the official application

  1. Open the Teach For India application portal and follow its Apply Now route to the eligibility checker.

  2. Read the eligibility questions and provide accurate information about your qualifications and applicant status.

  3. Complete the application with your achievements, interests, experiences and motivation for teaching.

  4. Follow the instructions shown in your application and save the submission confirmation. Monitor the contact channel you provide for further steps.

The portal describes an online application followed, for shortlisted candidates, by an assessment centre. Activities include sample teaching, a group activity, a critical-thinking assessment and an interview. The assessment centre may be attended online or in person, depending on convenience and location.

Decide whether you can make the two-year commitment

Previous teaching experience is not compulsory, but availability matters. Teach For India does not permit other professional or academic engagements during the Fellowship and says it does not currently offer deferrals. Consider your graduation timetable, relocation needs and existing commitments before submitting.

If you are looking for support to pay course fees while remaining enrolled in your present programme, compare the options in the DekhoCampus scholarship directory. This Fellowship has a different purpose: full-time work in a classroom with training and leadership development.

Frequently asked questions

Can a final-year student apply for the 2027 Fellowship?

Yes, provided graduation will be complete by June or July 2027 and the citizenship and first-application requirements are met.

Do I need a teaching qualification or previous classroom experience?

The official FAQs say prior teaching experience is not required. Teach For India provides training and development; applicants must still meet the published eligibility requirements and pass selection.

Will everyone receive ₹12,600 as an additional allowance?

No. The relocation allowance ranges from ₹6,000 to ₹12,600 depending on placement city and applies to Fellows relocating from their home city. Eligibility begins after moving to the placement city.

Can I continue another job or academic programme?

No. The Fellowship is a two-year full-time commitment, and the official FAQs do not permit other professional or academic engagements during it.

Is 1 November the deadline for the current application round?

Yes. The official portal lists 11:59 PM IST on Sunday, 1 November 2026. Do not interpret the wider selection-cycle dates as permission to submit after this deadline.

title: Nirankari Rajmata Scholarship 2026-27: Apply by Speed Post by 30 November
amount: Tuition support up to ₹75,000 per year
eligibility: First-year students in the listed professional courses in India, with at least 90% in Class 12, family income not above ₹5 lakh a year and admission through a competitive written test. Eligible previous beneficiaries can seek renewal. Read the course, exclusion and document rules below.
description:
Start with the admission and income checks

Fresh applications are for the first year of the courses named in the scheme: engineering, medicine in allopathic, Ayurvedic or homeopathic streams, architecture, MBA/PGDM, law, journalism and mass communication, and the specified CA/CFA routes. The official scheme document describes CA eligibility using CPT and CFA using a Foundation Test. If your qualification uses a different examination name, ask the foundation before assuming equivalence.

You need an admission offer, at least 90% in Class 12 and annual family income of ₹5 lakh or less. Admission must be through a competitive written test at a recognised institution. The foundation assesses both merit and financial need; applying is not a promise of funding.

What the tuition award covers

The annual ceiling is ₹75,000 per student, for tuition only. Renewal applicants normally need at least 75% in their subsequent annual examinations and must remain eligible. Support is reconsidered each year. In the final year, 75% of the approved fee is released first; the remaining 25% depends on receipt of the final-year marksheet and the foundation’s feedback form.

Prepare the packet before you post it

Open the foundation’s scholarship page for the current checklist and 2026-27 application form. Fill the form in block letters in your own handwriting and attach a recent photograph.

  • Include Class 10 onward academic records, Class 10 and 12 pass certificates, admission evidence and the latest fee receipts.

  • Provide the prescribed family-income evidence. An income certificate must have been issued within three months before submission.

  • Obtain the institution’s certificate covering other scholarships and the admission route, and complete the affidavit in the form.

  • Follow the checklist for identity records, family bank statements and the student’s account details where reimbursement is sought. Previous beneficiaries should include their earlier award letter.

Self-attest the required copies, tick the checklist and check that the applicant’s name matches across documents. Keep the original records available if the committee calls you for an interview.

Send it early enough to arrive by 30 November

Use Speed Post only, addressed to: Education Department, Sant Nirankari Charitable Foundation, 80-A, Avtar Marg, Sant Nirankari Colony, Delhi 110009, India. The official closing date is 30 November 2026; the guidelines say applications will not be received after it. A last-day dispatch may arrive too late.

Retain a copy of the complete packet and its tracking number. For course-equivalence or document questions, contact the foundation at sncf@nirankarifoundation.org. You can also explore other scholarship options, but check this scheme’s restriction on receiving another scholarship before accepting overlapping support.

Questions about the postal application

Can I submit this scholarship form online?

No. The published 2026-27 instructions require the completed application and documents by Speed Post. The website provides downloads, not an online submission route.

Is ₹75,000 guaranteed to every eligible student?

No. It is the annual tuition-support ceiling. The foundation’s committee decides assistance after assessing eligibility, merit and financial need.

Can I apply with exactly ₹5 lakh family income?

The official scheme sets the limit at not more than ₹5 lakh annually from all sources. You must still meet the other conditions and provide the required income evidence.

title: Top Class Education Scholarship for Students with Disabilities 2026-27: Eligibility and NSP Deadline
provider: Department of Empowerment of Persons with Disabilities, Government of India
amount: Fee reimbursement and allowances under official rules
eligibility: Indian students with benchmark disabilities of at least 40% may be eligible if they study a full-time graduate or postgraduate degree or diploma at an institute on the government’s notified list. The scheme’s family income ceiling is ₹8 lakh a year. Check the institute list and documents before applying.
description:
A place at a recognised college is not enough for this award. The Top Class Education Scholarship for Students with Disabilities is tied to a specific government-notified list of institutes, and it supports eligible students in full-time graduate or postgraduate degree or diploma study there. Before collecting documents, check the institute and course in the official DEPwD guidelines. This page was prepared by DekhoCampus’s AI editorial profile, Geethika Reddy, using the National Scholarship Portal’s current scheme listing and the linked government guidelines, checked on 23 October 2026.

Who can apply?

The guidelines require an Indian national with benchmark disability of at least 40% and a valid disability certificate. The family income ceiling is ₹8 lakh per year. The course must be a full-time graduate or postgraduate degree or diploma at one of the notified institutes of excellence. Distance, part-time and weekend courses are excluded. The scheme requires a UDID or UDID enrolment and Aadhaar-based authentication as specified in the official rules.

Do not assume that meeting these conditions guarantees a scholarship. The government guidelines provide 300 slots, including renewals, with 50% reserved for female candidates. Check the notification and the institute’s records before submitting an application.

What does the award cover?

The guidelines set different caps and supporting-document rules for each component. The amounts below are ceilings, not an automatic cash payment. Reimbursement depends on actual eligible costs and verification.

Deadline and application route

The National Scholarship Portal’s 2026-27 scheme listing shows 31 October 2026 as the student application closing date for Top Class Education for Students with Disabilities. Apply through NSP. Institute and state verification follow the student submission stage; do not treat their later dates as extra time to apply.

Match your identity, bank and disability details across documents before submitting. Check your institute’s name against Annexure I of the guidelines, then retain the submitted application and acknowledgement. If your college is not on that list, review the distinct Post-Matric Scholarship for Students with Disabilities and its own eligibility rules instead of assuming the two schemes are interchangeable.

Questions students ask

Is this the same as the Post-Matric disability scholarship?

No. Top Class Education is restricted to notified institutes of excellence and has a different support structure. Compare both official guideline sections before choosing a scheme.

Can a student at any private college apply?

Only if the college is on the notified institute list and the student meets the other conditions. The college name and course should be checked against the official list, not just a search result.

Does the 31 October deadline apply to institute verification too?

No. NSP labels it as the student application closing date. The portal lists separate verification stages.

title: Vidyasamunnathi Higher Secondary Scholarship 2026-27: Apply by 7 November
provider: Kerala State Welfare Corporation for Forward Communities
amount: ₹4,000 per year for selected students
eligibility:
For students from non-reserved forward communities in Kerala studying in Class 11 or 12 at a government or aided school in the state. You need at least B+ or 70% in SSLC or an equivalent examination, annual family income no higher than ₹4 lakh, and an active savings account in your own name.

The guidelines exclude recipients of other central or state government scholarships or stipends, with an exception for e-grantz. Read the applicable conditions before applying.
description:
A school certificate in the wrong format can hold up an otherwise eligible application. For Kerala's Vidyasamunnathi Higher Secondary Scholarship 2026-27, use the prescribed certificate completed by your school and submit the online form by 7 November 2026. The award is ₹4,000 a year for selected students, not an automatic payment to everyone who applies.

Check your school and SSLC result first

This category is for Class 11 and 12 students from non-reserved forward communities in Kerala. You must study at a government or government-aided school in the state and have at least B+ or 70% in SSLC or an equivalent examination. Annual family income from all sources must not exceed ₹4 lakh.

Read the official 2026-27 higher-secondary guidelines before choosing the category. Students receiving other central or state government scholarships or stipends are excluded, except for e-grantz. The corporation gives priority to lower-income applicants, and awards depend on available funds.

Get the school certificate in the right format

Download the higher-secondary institution certificate and ask your school authorities to complete it. The document checks your class, institution and qualifying-examination result. An informal school letter is not a substitute for the prescribed form.

The upload list also includes:

  • A family-income certificate issued by the Village Officer in the name of the household head shown on the ration card. An individual-income certificate is not accepted.

  • The specified caste proof: a Village Officer certificate recording caste, or the caste entry on the SSLC certificate.

  • Your SSLC or equivalent marksheet and the first page of the SSLC certificate.

  • The first page of your bank passbook, with the account number, IFSC and branch clearly readable.

  • Copies of pages 1 and 2 of the ration card that includes you.

Use an active savings account in your own name at a nationalised or scheduled bank. Check the account details against the passbook; the guidelines place responsibility for incorrect payment details on the applicant.

Submit a new application for 2026-27

The corporation's current application announcement confirms 7 November as the online deadline. It does not state a closing hour, so finish before the final day if you can.

  1. Open the official Samunnathi portal. Register if you are new; existing users should use their registered username and password.

  2. Complete your profile, select the higher-secondary scholarship for 2026-27 and fill in the application.

  3. Upload the required scans, review the details and submit. Keep copies of the application and documents.

A fresh scholarship application is required each year. Last year's form will not be considered for this year's assistance. Applicants do not need to post copies to the corporation after submitting online.

Vidyasamunnathi higher-secondary FAQs

Can I apply if I study at a private unaided school?

This category's guidelines cover government and aided schools in Kerala. A private unaided school does not meet that institution condition.

Is the ₹4,000 scholarship paid every month?

No. ₹4,000 is the annual scholarship amount for selected higher-secondary students. Selection depends on the scheme conditions and available funding.

Do I need to register again if I applied last year?

Use your existing registered username and password. You still need to submit a fresh scholarship application for 2026-27.

Can I send the documents by post instead of applying online?

No. Submit the application and scans through the official portal by 7 November 2026. The guidelines say applicants need not send copies by post after applying online.

Students in Classes 8 to 10 should check the separate Vidyasamunnathi high-school scholarship. For other levels, browse the scholarship directory.

title: SDEF India Scholarship 2026-27: Eligibility, Award and Application
amount: Up to ₹50,000 per academic year
eligibility: First-year full-time professional undergraduate students in India for 2026-27; at least 80% (or equivalent CGPA) in Class XII; annual family income no more than ₹12 lakh; and the applicable entrance-exam requirement. SDEF excludes students with a gap year after Class XII, part-time students, and those already in year two or later. Eligible programmes include engineering, medicine, dentistry, nursing, pharmacy, architecture and veterinary science.
description:
A student who cleared Class XII with strong marks but took a drop year should pause before applying: the Swami Dayanand Education Foundation explicitly excludes gap-year applicants from its 2026-27 India Scholarship. The same check matters for second-year students. This round is for new entrants to eligible full-time professional undergraduate degrees, and the application window closes on 31 October 2026.

Check eligibility before collecting documents

The foundation requires at least 80% in Class XII (or equivalent CGPA) and annual family income of ₹12 lakh or less. It lists engineering, medicine, dentistry, nursing, pharmacy, architecture and veterinary programmes. The applicable entrance threshold also matters: the published examples include JEE Main AIR 50,000 or below, JEE Advanced AIR 40,000 or below, NEET UG AIR 50,000 or below, and NATA 100 marks or above. For other eligible programmes, check the relevant recognised examination rule on the foundation’s eligibility page. A qualifying score is one condition, not a promise of selection.

What the award pays

SDEF states that the annual award is up to ₹50,000. Renewal can continue for up to four academic years, but it is reviewed each year against continued enrolment and academic performance. The funds go directly to the college or university for approved education expenses; students should not expect a transfer to a personal account. The foundation weighs merit, financial need, circumstances and application authenticity when choosing recipients.

Apply through the foundation

Start from the official India Scholarship page and select the fresh-applicant route, not the renewal form. Prepare your Class X and XII marksheets, entrance scorecard, admission letter, college identification, current fee receipt, income proof, a utility bill and the signed SDEF Scholar Pledge. The foundation also lists a photograph, Aadhaar and residence photographs among required uploads; agricultural or loan documents may apply to your circumstances. Read the current checklist before submitting, because incomplete applications are not reviewed.

The foundation says applications must be submitted online, not by post or email. It allows a saved form to be completed later, but the submission itself must be made before the deadline. If you encounter a document or portal problem, use the scholarship support contact on the official page.

Before starting the form, check four gates together: your programme must be on the foundation’s eligible list, your Class XII score must be at least 80% or its stated equivalent, annual family income must not exceed ₹12 lakh, and you must meet the relevant entrance-exam rule. title: North South Foundation Scholarship 2026-27: Apply Online and Send Documents
amount: ₹15,000-₹30,000 per year, depending on course
eligibility: For students admitted to the courses listed in NSF’s 2026-27 norms: regular or lateral-entry BE/BTech, engineering diploma, MBBS, and four-year integrated BA/BSc-BEd at NCERT Regional Institutes of Education. Academic marks, entrance ranks, state-based family-income limits and gap-year rules apply. MBBS applicants must attend a government medical college; private engineering and diploma colleges have branch restrictions.
description:
Match your course, entrance rank and annual award

The 2026-27 rules cover five course routes. Use your actual entrance-rank card when checking the limits, rather than a percentile or an estimated rank. The following combines the course-specific rank rules with the annual scholarship amount:

Course route

These are annual awards. Continued support is subject to renewal and academic performance. For a course or entrance route that does not match the table, ask the chapter coordinator before assuming eligibility.

Check marks, school fees and the income group

The foundation specifies at least 80% in Class 10 and Class 12, and at least 80% in diploma studies where applicable. A diploma applicant joining after Class 10 should confirm the documents required for that entry route with the chapter. Government-school students receive preference. For private schooling in Classes 10-12, the published school-fee limit is ₹50,000 a year.

The annual family-income ceiling depends on NSF’s state grouping:

  • ₹2 lakh: Bihar, Jharkhand, Odisha, Chhattisgarh, Uttar Pradesh, Madhya Pradesh, Rajasthan, Assam, Manipur, Meghalaya, Mizoram, Nagaland, Tripura, Arunachal Pradesh, and Jammu and Kashmir.

  • ₹2.25 lakh: Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, West Bengal, Punjab, Uttarakhand, Himachal Pradesh, Haryana, Sikkim, Andaman and Nicobar Islands, Daman and Diu, Puducherry, and Ladakh.

  • ₹2.5 lakh: Karnataka, Tamil Nadu, Kerala, Maharashtra, Gujarat, Goa, Delhi, Chandigarh, and Lakshadweep.

Use the official 2026-27 scholarship norms for the applicable ceiling. If your home location is not clearly covered by the grouping, ask NSF to confirm it instead of choosing a neighbouring state’s limit.

Private-college and gap-year conditions matter

For MBBS, only government medical colleges qualify under the current norms. Private engineering-college eligibility is restricted to specified branches. For BE/BTech, the list covers Computer Science, Electrical and Electronics, Electronics and Communication, Cyber Security, Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning, Data Science, Automobile, Applied Electronics and Instrumentation, and Metallurgical Engineering.

The private-college diploma list differs: Electrical, Mechanical, Automobile, Applied Electronics and Instrumentation, Metallurgical, Computer Science, and Artificial Intelligence and Data Science. Match your official branch name against NSF’s list; a related-sounding specialisation should be confirmed with the chapter.

Up to two years of gap after Class 12 or its equivalent are allowed for four-year BE/BTech, MBBS and the specified integrated BEd route. Lateral-entry engineering does not permit a gap. Engineering diploma applicants may join after Class 10 or Class 12, but must join without a gap after the qualifying stage they use. The provider’s student eligibility guide explains these distinctions.

Complete the online form and the paper submission

  1. Open the North South Foundation scholarship portal. New applicants can use the New Student option; existing account holders can sign in.

  2. Use an email address you can regularly access. The portal sends communications to that address.

  3. Enter your academic, admission, entrance-rank and family-income details carefully, then submit by 31 October 2026.

  4. Prepare the hard-copy application and required supporting documents. Self-attest the copies as instructed and confirm any college declaration requirements with your chapter.

  5. Send the hard copy to your chapter coordinator within a week of online submission. Arrange delivery so it reaches the chapter no later than 15 November 2026, and retain dispatch and delivery evidence.

Do not assume that an online acknowledgement means the paper requirement has been completed. For application or chapter queries, use the provider’s published support address, indiascholarships@northsouth.org.

What happens after applying?

Local chapters review applications and may shortlist students for interviews before recommending candidates. Further review and approval follow. The award depends on merit, financial need and available resources. NSF says exceptional hardship cases may be considered individually, but an exception should not be treated as an entitlement.

Keep your submitted records and monitor messages from the chapter. If selected, follow the renewal instructions in later years and maintain the academic standards required by the foundation.

Questions applicants should settle before submission

Can I wait until 15 November to register online?

No. Online registration closes on 31 October 2026. The 15 November date is for receipt of hard copies at chapters, and NSF also asks applicants to send them within a week of applying online.

Does every selected student receive ₹30,000?

No. The published annual amount is ₹30,000 for MBBS, ₹25,000 for the eligible engineering-degree and integrated BEd routes, and ₹15,000 for engineering diploma students.

Can a private-college MBBS student apply under these norms?

The 2026-27 general scholarship rules restrict MBBS eligibility to government medical colleges. The branch-based private-college provision applies to engineering and diploma courses.

Is this the government National Scholarship Portal?

No. This is North South Foundation’s own scholarship application system. Government schemes have separate applications. For example, eligible Northeast students can assess the Ishan Uday scholarship separately and check its restrictions on receiving other funding.

deadline: 22 November 2026, 11:55 pm New Zealand time, or earlier if filled
description:
Indian students planning to start at Auckland University of Technology in Semester 1, 2027 can apply for its South Asia scholarship. The current round closes at 11:55 pm on 22 November 2026, New Zealand time, or earlier if all places are filled. Start with your course offer: a scholarship application does not replace admission.

Choose the award for your study level

Study level

First-year tuition contribution

Undergraduate bachelor’s degree

NZ$10,000

Eligible master’s study, including certificates or diplomas leading to a master’s

NZ$7,000

Support lasts one year. Doctoral programmes are excluded. These are tuition contributions, not a promise to pay all study and living expenses. Work out the remaining tuition, accommodation, travel and other costs before accepting an offer.

Check your AUT offer before starting the form

Applicants must be new international fee-paying students from an eligible South Asian country, including India. A valid conditional or unconditional offer is required. Previous AUT students and students who have already started there cannot apply.

The South Asia scholarship regulations also set programme-length, full-time enrolment, residency and sponsorship conditions. Compare them with your exact offer rather than relying only on the scholarship’s name. Meeting the conditions does not guarantee selection.

Use the Semester 1 application route

The official AUT scholarship portal identifies the current form as Semester 1, 2027. It accepts one international-scholarship application for consideration by relevant panels; a successful applicant receives one scholarship. Do not submit through an unrelated faculty or accommodation form.

  1. Keep your AUT offer and student ID ready.

  2. Prepare your latest academic transcript, its grading scale and completion evidence.

  3. Open the official portal and select Apply Here. Check that the displayed intake matches your intended start.

  4. Complete the form and upload the required documents before the closing date. Keep the submission confirmation.

The deadline uses New Zealand time. Set your reminder accordingly if applying from India, and leave time to resolve upload or account problems. The earlier-closure condition means waiting until the last day is risky.

Plan for the fee balance

AUT applies the scholarship to tuition after the recipient accepts the award and university place and pays the remaining fees required. Read the offer’s conditions before arranging payment. For later intakes, return to AUT’s international scholarship page and select the matching round.

You can also compare other options in the DekhoCampus scholarship directory.

Questions before applying

Is this open to students from India?

Yes. India is included in the South Asia group, but applicants must also satisfy the student, programme and offer requirements.

Does every postgraduate applicant receive NZ$10,000?

No. The current postgraduate award is NZ$7,000. NZ$10,000 is the undergraduate amount, and both awards are competitive.

Can I wait until 22 November to apply?

The portal allows the round to close earlier when places fill. Submit a complete application as soon as you are ready.

Is the scholarship a payment for living expenses?

No. It is a first-year tuition contribution. Budget separately for expenses outside that contribution.

description:
How much support can a student receive?

The scheme guidelines linked from NSP specify an annual academic allowance of ₹3,500 for day scholars and ₹7,000 for hostellers. These are annual amounts, not monthly payments. The higher rate depends on qualifying as a hosteller under the scheme; submitting a form does not itself confirm an award.

Student submission and verification have different deadlines

The 2026-27 Sikkim SC Class 9 and 10 entry on the official NSP scheme directory separates the stages below. Choose State Scheme and State of Sikkim to find the relevant entry.

Stage

Defective application verification

For a student who has not yet applied, 31 October is the date that matters. Do not treat an institute or officer verification date as an extension of the student window.

Apply through NSP and keep your school involved

Keep your existing identity, income and school records handy while filling the form. The document fields shown in your NSP application determine what you must provide; a general preparation checklist is not a scheme-specific list of compulsory uploads.

  1. Open the National Scholarship Portal and use its student registration or login route.

  2. Find the Sikkim pre-matric scholarship for SC students studying in Classes IX and X. Check the academic year and scheme name before proceeding.

Questions families often ask

Can a Class 8 student use this SC scholarship?

Is income of exactly ₹2.50 lakh within the limit?

Yes. The rule says annual parental or guardian income must not exceed ₹2.50 lakh. The income details still need to meet the scheme’s verification requirements.

Can I apply for the first time on 16 November?

No. NSP lists 31 October as the student application deadline. The November dates relate to verification stages.

Can I receive another educational scholarship at the same time?

The linked guidelines do not allow simultaneous receipt of another educational scholarship for Classes 1 to 10. If you hold another award, discuss the choice with your school before proceeding.

Who can apply under the DNHDD SC scheme?

This is the pre-matric route for Scheduled Caste students, not the separate ST or OBC scholarship. You should be a DNHDD domicile studying full-time in Class 9 or 10, with parent or guardian income of no more than ₹2.5 lakh a year. The Ministry’s SC pre-matric scheme sets out these class and income conditions.

The specifications linked to the DNHDD scheme cover government schools and schools recognised by the government or an approved education board. Ask the school to confirm recognition and your eligibility before submitting.

Keep the student deadline separate from verification

The 2026-27 NSP directory gives different dates for submitting an application and completing later checks. Select Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu to find the SC pre-matric entry.

Stage

Closing date

Student application

31 October 2026

Defective application verification

15 November 2026

Institute verification

15 November 2026

DNO/SNO/MNO verification

30 November 2026

The November dates are not extra time to start a new student application. Submit within the October window, keep the acknowledgement and follow up with your school if the application needs correction or verification.

What amount should your family expect?

The Ministry’s national schedule lists consolidated annual support of ₹3,500 for day scholars and ₹7,000 for SC hostellers under the national framework, effective from 2022-23. However, the DNHDD entry on NSP links to specifications labelled 2019-20 with an older monthly allowance and book-grant structure.

Do not add the old monthly allowance to the newer annual amount. Ask the school or UT scholarship authority which rate will be used for your 2026-27 sanction. Until that is confirmed, treat the amount as unresolved for your application rather than promised income.

Apply through your NSP student account

Use the official NSP Students page for One Time Registration and the scholarship login. NSP requires an OTR number. Its student page provides the fresh and renewal application route and status checks.

  1. Confirm your domicile, caste, class and income details with the school.

  2. Sign in through NSP and choose the matching DNHDD SC pre-matric scheme for 2026-27, if it is offered for your profile.

  3. Complete the form and provide the documents requested in your application. Review names, bank details and school information carefully.

If you already receive another scholarship, disclose it to the school. NSP’s general rules for combining awards remain subject to the conditions of each scheme; do not assume a second payment is permitted automatically.
